articleTitle: Design of Quasi-Optical Microwave Pulse Compressor with Laser-Driven GaAs Switch
abstract: Quasi-optical microwave pulse compressor with laser-driven GaAs switch has been designed and developed. The compressor is based on three-mirror travelling wave resonator and a disk-shaped GaAs wafer, which serves as a switch activated by a picosecond 532 nm laser with pulse energy up to 50 mJ. The wafer with a diameter of 150 mm and a thickness of 0.6 mm is installed at Brewster's angle to the operating wave traveling in the resonator, that almost eliminates loss corresponding to parasitic reflection from the wafer. Resonator is thermostabilized in order to maintain its resonant frequency with precision of 0.5 MHz, which is less than the resonance bandwidth amounted to 2.7 MHz for the operating mode with resonant frequency of 170 GHz and the Q-factor of 6*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>. Stabilization of temperature is provided by water circulating in channels inside the resonator base. According to results of preliminary experiments with GaAs switch, in the developed compressor a formation of nanosecond and sub-nanosecond output microwave pulses with compression ratio of about 40 is achievable. For the input pulses produced by 170 GHz, 1 MW gyrotron, maximum power of output compressed microwave pulses is expected to be of about 40 MW. According to our estimations, this level of output radiation pulse power will not lead to development of surface microwave discharge at any element of compressor resonator in vacuum conditions.

articleTitle: Relative Thermodynamic Stabilities of Sc-Containing Surface Configurations in Scandate Cathodes
abstract: Scandate cathodes have been reported to exhibit superior emission properties to other classes of thermionic cathodes. However, a deeper understanding of their fundamental operating behavior is crucial before widespread technological integration. There remains no consensus as to the role of Sc in improved emission. Extensive characterization of scandate cathodes reveals that all high-performance cathodes contain W nanoparticles of a characteristic shape. Surface configurations containing Sc in variety of arrangements were evaluated by ab initio approaches at finite temperature and relative surface excess free energies compared. It was observed that no surface containing both Ba and Sc exhibited a particularly low surface energy, although several with Sc or O/Sc had very low surface energies. However, none of these high-stability configurations exhibit work functions comparable to those attributed to scandate cathodes.

articleTitle: Observation of Low-Frequency Oscillations in W-Band Gyro-TWTs Caused by Weak and Strong Plasma
abstract: Observation of the low-frequency oscillations (LFOs) in our designed W-band lossy-circuit loaded gyrotron travelling wave tubes (gyro-TWTs) caused by residual gas ionization is reported in this paper. The gas released from the lossy dielectric is ionized by colliding with the high-energy gyrating electrons. Then weak plasma is generated and the vacuum in the tube decreases to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">–5</sup> Pa. An LFO spectrum of 13 MHz was observed in this condition. However, when the vacuum is worse further, an LFO spectrum of 50–125 MHz was observed formed by the strong plasma excited near the cathode region. Both the above-mentioned plasma leads the beam current to be unstable and deteriorate the gyro-TWT performance.

articleTitle: Design of an Electron Gun and PPM Focusing System for Low-voltage W-band TWTs
abstract: This paper displays a design of an electron Gun and PPM focusing system with 12.6 kV for W-band TWTs. The focus electrode dimensions are swept to optimize the emitted cathode current and gunpot by employing Opera 3D technology. Using this design, a well-focused electron beam can be obtained.

articleTitle: The Low-Voltage Magnetrons with Two Energy Outputs
abstract: This paper presents the results of the theoretical and experimental research directed to creating the low-voltage X- and Ku-ranges magnetrons with two energy outputs. The application of the second (reactive) energy output in a design of a conventional magnetron has enabled additionally to realize the frequency tuning (adjustment) mode and the frequency stabilization using a high-Q resonator in the reactive output. It has shown that an offered design of the magnetron possesses improved frequency performances (for example, the frequency stability is not worse than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>, and the frequency tuning (or adjustment) can be realized in the band 250 MHz in the X-range and 110 MHz in the Ku-range). The experimental results show that the magnetrons with two energy outputs have broader functional possibilities for their practical application.

articleTitle: Research for High Power G-Band Transformed Folded Waveguide Pulsed Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: As Terahertz technology developed, the research for G-band folded waveguide Traveling Wave Tube (FWTWT) requires higher power and wider band. The design simulation and experiment on 0.22THz pulsed FWTWT was presented, including electronic-optical system, transformed folded waveguide slow wave structure (TFWSWS) and input/output windows system. By the measurement, the G-band pulsed TFWTWT can reach over 70W output power with 5.5GHz -3dB bandwidth at 0.5% duty cycle. The maximum output power is about 75W in frequency 218GHz, the gain is 29.62dB.

Author Keywords: transformed folded waveguide slow wave structure

articleTitle: A Broadband TE01Mode Input Coupler for Ka-band MW-level Coaxial Gyrotron Travelling Wave Tubes
abstract: In this paper, the design and measurement of a broadband TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode input coupler for Ka-band MW-level coaxial gyrotron travelling wave tubes (gyro-TWTs) are presented. The measured results agree well with the simulated results. The measured -10 dB reflection bandwidth is 4.7 GHz (27.5-32.2 GHz), and the transmission is over -0.5 dB in this band.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Traveling Wave Tube Amplifier Circuit using Elastic Averaging Precision Alignment Techniques
abstract: A Ka-band Serpentine waveguide (SWG) Traveling Wave Tube (TWT) circuit using the elastic averaging precision alignment techniques was designed and fabricated. The alignment accuracy of the assembled circuit was evaluated using a scanning coordinate measurement machine (CMM) with key circuit RF and electron beam features achieving an RMS alignment value of 7 microns

articleTitle: Preliminary Study of Array Magnetrons Phase-Locking Performance Measurement Based on Perturbation Theory
abstract: This paper proposes an experimental scheme to measure the performance of magnetrons, which has a phase-locking mechanism, based on perturbation theory. The content contains the theory analysis and preliminary simulation. The preliminary results verify the feasibility of measuring the phase-locking performance through experiments.

articleTitle: High Field Emission Performance of Carbon Nanotube Bundle Field Emitters
abstract: Carbon Nanotubes (CNTs) have become one of the best candidates for field emitters in recent years. Their ultra-high aspect ratio and good electrical conductivity give them excellent field emission (FE) performance. However, the quick degradation of CNT field emitters leads to their short lifetime, which limits their performance in high current and long duty cycle applications. There have been many attempts to improve the lifetime of CNT field emitters through various fabrication methods, but they all have some limitations such as uneven length. In this study, a new method is proposed to increase the lifetime of CNT emitter and improve the performance, by binding individual CNT together to form a more uniform CNT bundle arrays with lower electrical resistance. This type of CNT field emitter has proved to have a great potential in applications with high current and long continuous operating time.

articleTitle: Prelimenary Investigation on the Explosive Field Emission Model Using Vircator Particle-In-Cell Simulation
abstract: Explosive field emission is vital to relativistic vacuum electronics, for it is the only method to generate high energy electron beam. In the theoretical explosive field emission model used in Particle-In-Cell simulation, there are three parameters that define explosive field emission: voltage rise time, threshold field, and residual field. However, the true effects of these three parameters are often not easy to comprehend for the particle distribution and space charge field in various vacuum electronics differ a lot. In this paper, we use Vircator as an example, which should be the simplest form of high power relativistic vacuum electronics. A comparison of two field emission threshold PIC simulations of Vircators are performed and results compared. We learn that field emission threshold is not as it literally implied, it is a time mark rather than a field mark.

articleTitle: Experiment of a High Fill Ratio Electro-Optical System for a Ka-Band Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: This paper reported the experiments of a high fill ratio pencil beam electro-optical system (EOS). This EOS is for a Ka-band modified angular log-periodic folded waveguide (MALP-FW) traveling wave tube (TWT). The designed operating voltage is 12.06 kV and the desired current is 102 mA. The particle tracking simulation shows the output current of the electron gun is 97.7 mA while it drops down to be 93.9 mA in experiment. The fill ratio in radius and the beam transparency are about 90% and 100%, respectively, in simulation. The obtained beam transparency in experiment is 88.29%.

articleTitle: Cherenkov Maser Amplifier Nonlinear Analysis and Simulations
abstract: Compact, high-power, and wide band amplifiers, operating in the GHz frequency regime, have a number of important applications, ranging from rf communications with ground and airborne systems to electronic disruption. Amplifiers in this frequency range are key to achieving the necessary waveform diversity and agility for these applications. In this work the fundamental limits of the Cherenkov Maser Amplifier (CMA) in generating high-power levels over a wide frequency range is analyzed. In the CMA, a high-current, relativistic electron beam is injected and propagates in a dielectrically lined waveguide. The dielectric layer reduces the phase velocity of the hybrid TEM-TM mode of the wave guide to equal the electron beam velocity. This coupling allows for GW output powers throughout the 1–4 GHz range. Conversion efficiency can be enhanced by pre-modulating the electron beam or tapering the phase velocity along the length of the wave guide.

articleTitle: Research on Low-Frequency Oscillations Caused by Outgassing from Attenuated Dielectric
abstract: In this paper, stray electrons generated by outgassing from attenuated dielectric in the experimental measurement of W-band gyro-TWT are analyzed. The characteristics of stray electrons, such as trajectory and the frequency of low-frequency oscillations (LFOs), are simulated and discussed. The results are in good agreement with the experimental results. On this basis, the root of the instability of the whole tube performance in the test experiment is found, and it has important guiding significance for the follow-up project to put forward effective methods to suppress LFOs.

articleTitle: Dual Mini-TWT for Active Array Antenna
abstract: Motivated by the advent of disruptive flexible satellite payloads, Thales is radically revisiting its TWT architecture to offer cost efficient solutions with very low mass and dimensions for dense integration into active array antenna. These designs also achieve low power dissipation at all drive levels. They operate both Ku (10.7-12.75 GHz) and Ka (17.3-20.2 GHz) with a broad instantaneous bandwidth covering either the full Ku, or Ka band. We present specifications, technologies, performances and maturity of this new component.

articleTitle: Issues with the Explosive Field Emission Model in PIC Code-Unlimited Current Density
abstract: Fowler-Nordheim equation was originally developed to describe field emission from small tip, but now its form is widely used in describing various kinds of field emission macroscopic applications including high power microwave scenarios. In this article we test explosive field emission model in a particle-in-cell (PIC) code simulation of Vircator, and found as the externally applied voltage increases, the field emission current density also keep on increasing, to an extent that it exceeds experimentally possible value. The reason for this is that in the theoretical derivation of Fowler-Nordheim equation, an ideal current source capable of supplying infinite current was assumed, therefore there is no limitation of field emission current density.

articleTitle: Development Progress of a 220-GHz Extended Interaction Klystron
abstract: This paper introduces the development progress of a compact 220-GHz Extended Interaction Klystron (EIK). And the EIK can produce more than 100-W output power near the 220-GHz operating frequency, while the operating voltage is less than 20kV, the power bandwidth is more than 150MHz, the gain is more than 30dB, and the duty cycle is 5%. The subsequent optimization of EIK is in progress.

articleTitle: Effects of Magnetic Field on Stability and Attainable Power of VE Amplifiers
abstract: Theory and modeling of new discovered effects of magnetic focusing field on the stability, gain, and power of VE amplifiers is presented. The RF structure and e-beam circuit parameter matrices are computed for different magnetic focusing conditions and then the self-excitation thresholds are obtained from the Determinant equations [1]. A new formulation for the RF structure gain is derived and used for the found self-excitation thresholds. It is shown for the example <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K_{a}$</tex> -band serpentine structure that the optimum magnetic focusing allows significantly greater gain and power than the conventional focusing. The methods and analysis described here are essential for achieving high power and bandwidth of RF amplifiers.

articleTitle: Numerical Method for Coil Magnetic Field of Traveling-Wave Tube
abstract: The focusing system of traveling wave tube is used to control the electron beam to ensure good pass ability during the whole interaction process. Based on MTSS-MFS, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex> special simulation permanent magnet focusing system software developed by UESTC, a method for calculating coil magnetic field is studied in this paper. The maximum error of the calculated results is less than 3% and the average error is less than 1% compared with the result calculated by Maxwell, the mainstream industrial software.

articleTitle: Additive Manufacturing Methods for Millimeter-Wave Vacuum Electronics
abstract: We discuss progress on additive manufacturing (AM) methods for the fabrication of millimeter-wave (mmW) vacuum electronic (VE) devices. Polymer 3D printing is discussed for fabrication of light-weight RF body assemblies with many integrated RF components such as waveguide power couplers and power combiners. Stainless-steel binder-jetting is discussed for fabrication of high-power VE circuits in metal, combined with infiltration of the bulk metal with a filler metal (such as Cu) to increase the electrical and thermal conductivity to the high level needed for mmW circuits.

articleTitle: Characterization of Reflected RF Power in a Misaligned Ka-Band Serpentine Waveguide TWT
abstract: We present a study of the effects misalignments have in the assembly of the two halves of a Kaband serpentine waveguide TWT structure using the high frequency electromagnetic simulation software HFSS. The goal of the study is to determine manufacturing tolerances needed in the assembly process. We focus here on the reflected power as a function of frequency from simulations of various misalignments in the plane of the serpentine waveguide's beam tunnel.

articleTitle: Investigation on E-Band High Efficiency Folded Wave-Guide Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: A new E-band high efficiency folded waveguide traveling wave tube (TWT) is investigated by numerical simulation and fabrication experiments. The results show that the modified folded waveguide circuit achieves higher coupling impedance than conventional folded waveguide circuit with lower phase velocity. Comparing with conventional folded waveguide TWT, this new folded waveguide TWT obtained electron efficiency of more than 10% with lowered operation voltage and shortened circuit length. Fabrication experiments also have been carried out and the feasibility of the new circuit technology is proved.

articleTitle: Design of Triple-Gap Cavity Output Circuit for X Band Klystron
abstract: The triple-gap cavity technology is an important means to expand the bandwidth of the klystron output circuit. In order to realize 1 GHz output bandwidth for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex> band klystron, the equivalent circuit simulation of the triple-gap cavity is carried out. The actual cavity size is determined by the designed electrical parameters and the cold test model is processed. Based on the microwave network analysis theory and perturbation theory, a test method for the gap impedance of the triple-gap cavity was designed, and the output circuit of the klystron with a bandwidth of 1 GHz (9150 MHz-10150 MHz) was tested, which laid an important technical foundation for the development of broadband klystrons.

articleTitle: Susceptibility of Single-Surface Multipactor Driven by Non-Sinusoidal Transverse RF Electric Field
abstract: Single-surface multipactor discharges near a microwave window are a limiting factor in space-based microwave transmission systems. The mitigation of multipactor is of importance for signal transmission. Here a non-sinusoidal electric field, e.g., Gaussian waveform, is proposed to reduce the multipactor strength, and the corresponding susceptibility of multipactor versus the rf electric field amplitude is investigated via particle-in-cell simulations and multiple particle Monte Carlo simulations. The results show that, at a larger half peak width of a Gaussian waveform Δτ = 0.15T with T = 1 ns the rf period, the susceptibility of multipactor is similar to that of a single frequency sinusoidal waveform-driven multipactor. However, at a decreased half peak width Δτ = 0.07T, the multipactor strength decreases with increasing rf electric field amplitude, the unit growth rate is a closed curve in the plane of rf electric field amplitude and dc restoring electric field, implying the effectiveness of Gaussian waveform in mitigating the multipactor strength in real application.

articleTitle: Multipactor Susceptibility and Suppression in Microstripline Transmission Line
abstract: We present our recent progress in investigating multipactor, including predicting susceptibility, experimental validation, and suppression techniques. We developed a versatile high-power multipactor experimental apparatus that enables us to conduct various two-surface multipactor experiments in a parallel-plate microstripline structure over a broad frequency range from DC to 1.2 GHz. We used this experimental setup to validate multipactor susceptible zones predicted by our fast, approximate semianalytic resonance model. We also present results of research of approaches to partially or fully suppress two-surface multipactor. For example, high porosity surfaces are observed to reduce or fully suppress multipactor susceptibility via reducing the effective secondary electron yield (SEY) of surfaces. In a different approach, we investigate multitone excitations to disrupt the resonance coherence of two-surface multipactor, reducing its susceptibility.

articleTitle: Space Radar TWTs for new Applications
abstract: The changing environment and climatic changes require more and more sensitive instruments in space to monitor and if possible to predict changes and to be used as warning systems. These instruments can be optical or RF-based. For the RF solution, an array antenna with TR modules or a large reflector antenna with a high-power RF amplifier can be selected. This paper concentrates on the RF solution with traveling wave tube amplifiers.

articleTitle: Impact of the Patch Fields and Space Charge on the Shape of the Miram Curve
abstract: The emission current density versus temperature (J-T) curve of thermionic cathodes is often referred to as the Miram curve. The transition between the temperature-limited (TL) and full-space-charge-limited (FSCL) emission regions in a Miram curve is referred to as the “roll-off” or “Miram curve knee”. The shape of the Miram curve is an important figure of merit for thermionic cathodes. Cathodes with a sharp knee at a low temperature and flat saturated emission current are typically preferred. In this work, we use a periodic, equal-width striped (so-called “zebra crossing‘’) work function distribution as a model example, illustrating how the space charge and patch fields impact the shape of the Miram curve knee, including the smoothness and the temperature of the knee, as well as the flatness of the saturated emission current density. This study provides new understanding and a guide to the analysis of experimental Miram curves and to the design of thermionic cathodes used as electron sources in vacuum electronic devices (VEDs).

articleTitle: Preparation of SnOx Thin Films For Vacuum Electronic Amplifiers Applications
abstract: For vacuum electronic amplifiers applications, SnOx films were deposited by reactive radio frequency magnetron sputtering. Electrical properties of SnOx films have been studied as a function of oxygen partial pressure, annealing temperature, working pressure and sputtering power.

articleTitle: Investigation of Brewster Window for Broadband Terahertz Backward Wave Oscillator
abstract: This paper investigates a Brewster window applied in broadband terahertz backward wave oscillator, which can work in 250–600 GHZ frequency band range. Transmission characteristics of different window materials such as quartz, CVD diamond, sapphire, and aluminum nitride ceramic are simulated and compared.

articleTitle: Experiment on Radial Beam Angular Log-periodic Strip-line Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: In this paper, the hot testing experiments for radial beam angular log-periodic strip-line (ALSL) traveling wave tubes (TWTs) are investigated. The whole tube was assembled and welded for the planar strip-line slow wave structure (SWS) and the corresponding experiments were performed. Electron gun emission current 52mA, collector current 36mA, transmission rate of 69%. Experimental maximum output gain of 4.4dB, and the overall gain trend is consistent with the simulation results. The working capability of the radial beam TWT was verified rationally in the experiments.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study of a Sub-Terahertz Orthogonal Grating Waveguide for High-Order Mode Backward Wave Oscillators
abstract: The preliminary design of a sub-terahertz high-order mode (HOM) orthogonal grating waveguide (OGW) for multiple sheet-beam backward wave oscillators (BWOs) is presented in this paper. The dispersion characteristic of HOM OGW is simulated by using the Eigenmode Solver of the Computer Simulation Technology (CST). A 100-period OGW circuit is simulated, which indicates that the transmission and reflection coefficients are above -2 dB and below -10 dB in the frequency range of 168.8-223.2 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: DMLS Enables Rapid, Low-Cost Manufacture of an X-Band Klystron Circuit
abstract: Additive manufacturing has drawn considerable interest as a manufacturing technique for passive RF components such as antennae, filters, and waveguides. However, extending this work to high power active components could allow rapid and cost-effective manufacturing of tightly integrated and highly complex systems. Here we present a process for manufacturing a klystron circuit using copper-plated 3D-printed stainless steel. The resonance of each klystron cavity was determined before and after brazing. Results show consistent and accurate resonance within 5% of simulations.

articleTitle: Eigenmode Solution for Beam-Loaded Slow Wave Structures Based on Particle-In-Cell Simulations
abstract: We present a method to model hot slow wave structures based on finding the unit-cell's transfer matrix. The method considers the small-signal interaction between the electromagnetic guided field and the electron beam via three-dimensional (3D) particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations. We calculate the complex-valued wavenumbers of the hot modes in a serpentine waveguide near the synchronization point. The distribution of the calculated complex-valued wavenumbers agrees with the one predicted by the Pierce model. The results show that the gain calculated based on the proposed model very well matches the one calculated from 3D PIC simulations of the whole structure. The results also show that the proposed model is superior to the Pierce model on predicting the gain of long structures.

articleTitle: The Study on the Key Parameter in Beam-Wave Resynchronization Method of the Non-Periodic FW-SWS for TWTs
abstract: For improving the electronic efficiency, the beam-wave resynchronization (BWRS) method of non-periodic (NP) slow-wave structure (SWS) are proposed in our previous work, where a key parameter (ε) was defined to build the beam-wave synchronization (BWS) condition. How to obtain the accurate value of ε is introduced in this paper. For the concrete NP folded-waveguide SWS (FW-SWS), the ratio of ε and beam velocity is about 5.1% with the difference of the relative velocity smaller than 0.01%.

articleTitle: Impact of Asymmetric Beam Shapes on the Body Current and BWO Margin in Helix TWTs
abstract: The effects of asymmetric beam shapes, caused by geometric asymmetries of the electron gun or asymmetries of the magnetic focusing system, on the body current and the sensitivity to backward wave oscillations (BWO) are investigated by simulation. It is found that asymmetric beams can significantly increase the body current and the sensitivity to BWO.

articleTitle: Recent Advances on Magnetically Insulated Line Oscillator (MILO)
abstract: This paper reports the recent advances on the theory, simulation and experiments on the magnetically insulated line oscillator (MILO) at the University of Michigan. Using the Brillouin flow model, a new, general theory was developed and was applied to a cylindrical MILO with axial electron flow, including a rigorous derivation of the Buneman-Hartree (BH) condition, for the first time. It also reveals the unexpected feature that a MILO may operate at a lower current than that required for Hull cutoff. Using this theory, aided by the particle-in-cell codes ICEPIC and CST-Particle Studio (CST-PS), a MILO was designed for operation on the Michigan Electron Long Beam Accelerator (MELBA) at ~240-300 kV, < 10 kA, which is the lowest MILO operating current to-date. Our MELBA experiments consistently demonstrated performance as predicted by the theory and simulations. Notably, the experiments were observed to operate closer to the Hull cutoff (HC) condition than the BH condition. An analysis of other devices in the literature reveals this to be a common operating condition for MILO. The advancements made in this work have substantially improved the theoretical rigor of MILO design, approaching that for a magnetron.

articleTitle: Theoretical Research on a TM02 Mode Terahertz Extended Interaction Oscillator
abstract: An overmoded terahertz (THz) extended interaction oscillator (EIO) with high beam loading capability is presented. Through the reconstruction of the high-order mode field, a super-large beam processing mechanism is established. It proves that the overmoded operation oriented by increasing the circuit size has more potential technology expansions related to beam-wave energy conversion. This EIO is driven by annular electron beam with operating voltage 28.4kV and current 0.7 A. Beam with outside diameter 3.56mm and inside diameter 3.3mm is designed. Through particle in cell (PIC) simulation, the circuit is proved to achieve kilowatt-level output power at 0.1 THz when operating stably in TM02 mode.

articleTitle: COBRA DANE Radar Transmitter Group Replacement
abstract: In 2019, Diversified Technologies, Inc. (DTI) delivered a transmitter group replacement (TGR) for the COBRA DANE ground-based radar facility at Eareckson Air Station, Shemya Island, Alaska. This individual L-Band transmitter subsystem is part of the twelve transmitter groups housed at the facility. Each transmitter group energizes, controls, and protects eight high-power, ringbar type traveling wave tubes (TWTs). Individual RF outputs from each tube are input to a space-fed phased array antenna. As a result of this successful installation, the USAF awarded DTI a contract to build and deliver the remaining 11 transmitter groups in 2020.

articleTitle: Vacuum Electronics Industry Retrospective and Futurecast
abstract: An unvarnished recap of a 40-plus year career in plasma physics/vacuum electronics, the majority spent in the US vacuum tube industry. The good, the bad and the ugh, ugly. Happily, the number of experiences in the latter two categories are in the minority. Some observations are offered on key constituents of the community - suppliers, users, university, government/labs, along with a take on some technical achievements I was fortunate to be associated with, and some that remain to be realized. The paper concludes with some application and technology areas that could prove attractive for future R&D investment.

articleTitle: High Current p-i-n-nanoC Diamond Diodes for Electron Emission
abstract: Conventional electron sources utilize high temperatures or high electric fields to extract electrons from a solid where the emission current can be described by the thermionic Richardson-Dushman and the field emission related Fowler-Nordheim relation, respectively. A novel approach for electron sources can exploit aspects of diamond as an electronic material where n-type and p-type doping in conjunction with negative electron affinity properties allows engineering of p-i-n solid state diodes for direct electron emission. We prepared p-i-n-nanoC diamond diodes on single crystal diamond substrates by plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition and utilized a nitrogen incorporated nanostructured carbon (nanoC) layer as an electrical contact layer. The emitter structures were prepared using lithography to prepare mesa-etched structures with varying geometry. The final device was exposed to a hydrogen plasma that induced the negative electron affinity (NEA) properties of the devices. Application of a forward bias established a current through the device and the observation of light emission was an indication of bipolar transport and attributed to the free exciton recombination in diamond. With an increase in the diode current an increase in the electron emission current was observed. For a small emitter structure sized 1.2 x 0.22 mm a diode current of 1A corresponded to a current density of 408A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This diode current effected an electron emission current of about 0.7mA corresponding to an electron emission current density of 0.285A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Stepped Sub-THz Gyrotron Cavity with Improved Output Mode Purity
abstract: Stepped cavity resonators are used in terahertz gyrotrons for better mode selection. They can satisfy the resonance condition for two modes with different radial indices. Such sectioned resonators, or complex cavities, were analyzed in detail by several authors in the past. One common problem for such designs is the excitation of unwanted modes by both the stepped cavity structure and the cavity output taper. Mode conversion becomes especially a severe problem for higher order resonant modes in highly oversized resonators. We introduce ways to minimize the unwanted mode conversion in both, the stepped cavity as well as in the output taper.

articleTitle: A Novel Scheme to Reduce the Electron Loss and Power Amplification in an Axial Virtual Cathode Oscillator
abstract: In this study, reuse of the escaping electrons for the formation of the second virtual cathode (VC-2) was presented. To achieve this, a reflector made up of dielectric material was designed and installed inside the drift tube downstream region. the drifting electrons formed a VC-2 when they are accumulated at the surface of the dielectric reflector as a wall charge. Interestingly, the electromagnetic wave interacted with the charge of VC-2 and its amplitude is increased approximately four times than the conventional one. With the presented technique, the achievable vircator efficiency is more than 20 %.

articleTitle: Transmission Loss of a Millimeter Wave Pulse Through a Waveguide Window
abstract: Millimeter waves have become increasingly important in wireless communication today. It is well known that a waveguide window exhibits almost perfect transmission for the center frequency of millimeter waves. However, this might not be true for a pulsed wave. In this work, we study the transmission loss of a millimeter wave pulse centered at 35 GHz traveling through a rectangular waveguide window. The transmission function of a continuous wave within the bandwidth from 0 to 100 GHz has been obtained using the transfer matrix method. The millimeter wave of 35 GHz pulsed from 100 ps to 1 us in time domain has been Fourier transformed to the frequency domain so that the transmittance of the pulsed wave in the frequency domain can be calculated. The transmission loss has been analyzed for various pulse durations. After inverse Fourier transform of the transmittance in the frequency domain back to the time domain, one can compare the result with the incident pulse to see the pulse distortion and transmission loss. A finite difference time domain simulation has been performed to verify the calculated results by the transfer matrix method combined with Fourier transform. Detailed methodology and analysis of the study will be presented.

articleTitle: A Design of Measuring Module for the Loss of Clamping Rod in K-Band
abstract: Loss parameter of the clamping rod is the key indicator to measure the performance of the centralized attenuator. Measuring the loss of the clamping rod accurately is conducive to the design of attenuator. In this paper, the waveguide method is used to measure the loss of the K-band clamping rod, and a measuring module is designed. The electric field of TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode in rectangular waveguide can be used as an analog electric field to measure the loss of the clamping rod. The measuring module designed in this paper can measure the value of the loss of the clamping rod directly, and then obtain the distribution law of the loss.

articleTitle: Simulation of Copper Plating on Coupler Bellows Under Different Current Densities
abstract: Coupler bellows are important parts of superconducting cavity in free electron laser device. In order to improve the microwave transmission performance, copper film needs to be coated on the coupler bellows. In this paper, the distribution of current, overpotential and concentration of copper coating on bellows under different current density was analyzed. At low current, there were dynamic constraints in the copper plating process. With the increase of current, the local current density changed greatly along the cathode shape. According to the tertiary current density distributions, the copper ion concentration changed significantly. In the process of copper coating, it changed from charge transfer control to mixed (charge transfer and mass transfer) control.

articleTitle: Design of a Terahertz Multi-Beam BWO Based upon Sine Waveguide
abstract: A multi-beam backward wave oscillator (BWO) is presented by using a sine waveguide with three pencil beams to produce the high power terahertz wave. The dispersion properties of the slow-wave structure (SWS) are analyzed in detail. The transmission characteristic calculation shows that the transmission loss <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S21 > -5dB$</tex> and the reflection <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Sll < -20dB$</tex> over the operating frequency band (from 720 to 850 GHz). A 3-D particle-in-cell solver is applied to predict the device performance of the BWO. The investigation results demonstrate that this device can generate over 2.4 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> output power in the frequency range of 693–842 GHz by using a 5 mA pencil electron beam and adjusting the beam voltage from 18.7 kV to 39.8 kV.

articleTitle: A Novel Cold Characteristics Simulation for Wide-Band Helix TWTs
abstract: In this paper, cold circuit parameters of helix SWS like dispersion and impedance characteristics have been carried out using HFSS and CST microwave studio by varying of helix SWS parameters for X-Ku-band helix TWT. Analysis of helix SWS for APBN, Alumina, Diamond and Bariliya materials of dielectric support rods has been carried out for achieving broad bandwidth, high gain, high efficiency and high linearity of a space helix TWT. The present analytical results were also validated simulation with a good agreement.

articleTitle: Experimental Tests Results of 170 GHz Gyrotron-Driver for Frequency Locked MW Gyrotron
abstract: The problem of frequency stabilization is important for modern gyrotron application such as, for example, high gradient particle acceleration by powerful microwaves. We present experimental results of the test 20 kW/170 GHz tube, which is proposed as a source of external signal for 1 MW/170 GHz gyrotron. Frequency control of gyrotron-driver is organized by feedback control of anode voltage in triode magnetron injection gun, The spectrum width about 1 Hz has been obtained.

articleTitle: One Technological Process Design of Planar Slow Wave Structure by Using MEMS Method
abstract: A new method to massively fabricate planar SWS on Si wafer for compact TWT is introduced in this paper. The main technological process contains sacrificial layer, seed layer and electroplating copper. The traditional magnetron sputtering method to grow metal line faces the limit to get thicker metal. As a mature scheme, the electroplating can get a thicker metal layer (above 100 um) on the Si wafer. The dielectric block supporting metal meander line SWS is proved it can be a good candidate for small and compact TWT. The specific process of MEMS method for this SWS is presented and analyzed.

articleTitle: Two Benchmark Simulations of Intense Annular High-Current Electron Beam Generation, Acceleration, and Transport in a Smooth Cylindrical Waveguide Driven by the SINUS-6 Accelerator at UNM
abstract: The growing use of magnetically insulated coaxial diodes (MICDs) driven by high-current electron-beam accelerators has been inspired by their applications in O-type high-power microwave and millimeter-wavelength vacuum electron devices with linear slow-wave structures (SWSs) [1], [2]. Previous studies of MICDs with cold explosive plasma cathodes relied on experimental investigations [3] and analytical calculations [4], and thus, the underlying physics of MICDs was still not studied in computer simulation with modern particle-in-cell (PIC) codes. The scope of this study is to compare results of PIC simulations of intense electron beam generation, acceleration, and propagation in a smooth cylindrical waveguide with two benchmarked PIC codes, MAGIC and ICEPIC, and compare the simulation results with analytical calculations. We have previously used MAGIC simulations [1] to understand the process of hollow electron beam generation, acceleration, and propagation in a uniform magnetic field from an MICD. We have performed additional ICEPIC simulation to clarify the analytically derived Fedosov [4] solution with results of actual experiments [3] obtained from an MICD driven by the SINUS-6 accelerator [5]. All computer simulations are performed for an MICD with a cylindrical cathode with an outer radius of 9 mm and 11.15 mm and a grounded cylindrical smooth-walled waveguide with an inner radius 25.05 mm immersed in a strong axial magnetic field 3.2 T for input SINUS-6 voltages ranging 100–600 kV. Results of both MAGIC and ICEPIC simulations and subsequent analyses of hollow electron beam parameters in an MICD show that both the analytically calculated [4] “Fedosov” potential and “Fedosov” current almost perfectly correlate with obtained in numerical simulations maximum of axial kinetic energy distributions of the beam electrons and transported electron-beam current.

articleTitle: First-Principle Calculation of Tin Oxide for Resistive-Wall Amplifier
abstract: Resistive-wall amplifier is a kind of promising vacuum electronic device and coating of tin oxide can be the resistive wall. The crystal structure, band structure and dielectric function of rutile SnO2 and SnO2 with oxygen vacancy are studied by first-principle calculation for further research.

articleTitle: Frozen Mode in Three-Way Waveguide Slow-Wave Structure for Three-Mode Synchronization
abstract: We introduce a new geometry for serpentine waveguide slow-wave structures (SWS) for traveling-wave tubes (TWTs) with enhanced interaction impedance, or Pierce impedance, due to the stationary inflection point (SIP), i.e., a frozen mode. The three-way waveguide geometry, the serpentine ladder waveguide (SLWG), can be easily designed to exhibit such SIPs within the dominant TE10 mode of the waveguide cross section, below the first upper band-edge of the serpentine waveguide (SWG), where beam-wave synchronization typically occurs in SWG TWTs. These structures exhibit an enhanced interaction impedance due to the three-modes that are synchronized with an electron beam, and it may be useful for improving the power gain and basic extraction efficiency of millimeter- wave TWTs. Additionally, the introduced structure exhibits directional coupler-like behavior, which makes distributed power extraction (DPE) possible at frequencies at or near the introduced SIPs.

articleTitle: High Stability Klystron Modulator for Commercial Accelerator Application
abstract: Diversified Technologies, Inc. (DTI) designed and developed a high stability modulator system for a commercial linear accelerator application. The DTI modulator delivers significant advantages in klystron performance through highly reliable functionality as well as flicker- and droop-free operation from 50–500 µs up to 400 Hz (duty limited). The main assemblies on the DTI system consist of a controls rack, high voltage power supply (HVPS), modulator, and cooling manifolds for the modulator, high voltage power supply and klystron tube. Two HVPS (upgradeable to four) provide stable and accurate DC voltage which is used to drive a CPI VKP-8352C UHF-band pulsed klystron for the linear accelerator. A solid state series switch, based on DTI's patented design, provides both pulse control and arc protection to the klystron. Operating with four HVPS, the DTI modulator is able to operate at a maximum average power of ~750 kW at 105 kV, 47 A nominal. At the end of the initial contract, DTI provided two systems and a total of four HVPS (two of which are used with each system).

articleTitle: Frequency Tuning in a Gyrotron with a Cavity of Variable Cross Section
abstract: We describe an electrodynamic method based on azimuthally asymmetric cavities with a “close-to-circular” cross-section to provide a continuous frequency tuning in subterahertz gyrotrons operating on symmetric modes. A small mechanical change in the rotation angle of the moving “visor” changes the effective volume of the cavity and provides a relatively wide (several percent) bandwidth of continuous tuning of the gyrotron frequency.

articleTitle: D-Band Medium Power Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: D-band (141 - 175.8 GHz) is very attractive for high capacity wireless links. However, the low power available from solid state amplifiers is not sufficient to ensure long links with 99.99% availability in the most common rain zones. Traveling wave tubes have been extensively demonstrated as the solution for satisfying the link budget. At sub-THz frequencies their fabrication is difficult a nd expensive. Typically, t he 40 dB gain needed can be provided by two sections of slow wave structure separated by a sever. Due to the intrinsic low interaction impedance at sub-Thz frequencies, slow wave structures with high number of periods are needed. In case of metal SWS this determines long fabrication time and difficult a ssembly. This paper presents a short double corrugated waveguides for wide band (141 - 148.5 GHz) TWTs to provide about 26 dB gain and reduced fabrication difficulties.

articleTitle: Modeling of a Sheet Beam Electron Gun with High Compression Ratio
abstract: As a synthesis method, Ovcharov theory is used to rapidly design a sheet beam electron gun with potential applications in high power vacuum devices. In this paper, the 2D outlines of focusing electrode and anode using this method, were imported into CST Particle Tracking for 3D simulation. Although the optimized shape is not exactly the same as the theory result, the near-electron-beam spatial potential of the 3D model is comparable to that of the synthesis approach. Following discussing and optimizing of the structure, a sheet beam electron gun with a current density of 140 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was presented. The voltage of the gun is 42.7kV, its current is 2A and its area compression ratio is 20.5.

articleTitle: Scandate Cathode Performance in Xenon Discharge
abstract: Performance data on scandate cathodes in noble gas discharges is presented. These devices are used for ionization and neutralization in electric space propulsion. Two geometries were tested., one device was a 4 A plasma cathode for small satellite thrusters. The other device was a > 100 A plasma cathode for moving heavy payloads in space. The first device employed a 0.080-inch planar scandate cathode as electron source and was loaded to over 100 A/cm, The second employed a hollow scandate cathode with inside diameter 0.160-inch and length 0.5-inch and was loaded at 62 A/cm, It was found that the devices with scandate cathodes outperformed all other thermionic cathodes tested both in temperature efficiency (emission/cathode temperature) and electron efficiency (emission current/watts of input power). In one case a hollow scandate cathode delivered 100 A at 1059° Cb, at an anode voltage of less than 23 volts for an electron efficiency of 43.5 mA/watt. By contrast a hollow reservoir cathode with osmium/tungsten insert required 87 anode volts to extract 100 A of discharge current.

articleTitle: Photoinjector in IAP RAS: State and Prospects
abstract: At the Institute of Applied Physics of the Russian Academy of Sciences, a photoinjection electron accelerator is being developed, in which a step-by-step acceleration of particles up to an energy of about 20 MeV should be provided. The first 3.5 MeV section of the accelerator can be used to experimentally study promising regimes of terahertz radiation of short electron bunches. The low emittance bunches additionally accelerated in the second section are planned to be used for injection into the plasma accelerator system for the subsequent increase of the energy to a GeV level. In addition, work is underway to study new promising options for photocathodes.

articleTitle: Emission Test Facility for Dispenser Cathodes
abstract: Constructing a facility that would provide a viable, convenient method of testing the emission performance of dispenser cathodes under controlled conditions to provide meaningful consistent data.

articleTitle: Design of a High-frequency-system for a Dual-mode 220 GHz Sheet Beam TWT
abstract: In this paper, a dual-mode high-frequency-system was designed for a 220 GHz sheet beam traveling wave tube (SB-TWT). It is composed of a 100-period double staggered grating waveguide slow-wave structure (SWS) and two identical L-bend waveguide couplers loaded with Bragg reflectors and matching steps. Normally, the SB-TWT operates at one single mode. In this paper, the SWS is designed to operate at dual-modes. The effectiveness of the proposed idea is verified by the simulated dispersion relation and transmission property. The cold cavity analysis predicted that the bandwidth for the transmission coefficient of the high-frequency-system better than -3.0 dB was 58.9 GHz (232.8-291.7 GHz). The designed high-frequency-system is currently under machining using the nano-computer numerical control milling technique.

articleTitle: A Method for Solving the Output Current of Traveling Wave Tpube Electron Gun
abstract: The formula of electron gun output current establishes the relationship between cathode voltage, grid voltage, anode voltage, filament voltage and electron gun output current. Firstly, the relationship between cathode voltage, grid voltage, anode voltage, and the output current of electron gun is established based on the conductivity coefficient formula. Then, the relationship between filament voltage and electron gun output current is established through filament temperature. Finally, the output current formula of electron gun is obtained.

articleTitle: Concept of a Frequency-Tunable Sub-THz Gyrotron Based on the Partial Reflection of the Output Radiation from an External Mirror
abstract: We describe a concept of a sub-terahertz frequency-tunable gyrotron based on a combination of a low-Q irregular cavity and a frequency-tunable external reflector. Simulations predict possibilities for creation of gyrotrons with high (20% and higher) efficiencies provided in a wide (~10%)frequency band.

articleTitle: Design of Dynamic Variable Power with High Efficiency and Reliability for Ku-Band TWT
abstract: The traditional way to achieve the adjustment of the output power of the traveling wave tube(TWT) is to reduce the input power and keep the TWT in small signal working state, but it significantly affects the efficiency of the TWT.It is of great value to use the method of reducing cathode current to realize the high efficiency of both the state of saturation and the state when the power backs off the half of the state of saturation (the power back-off 3dB). When the emission current changes,the working state of the traveling wave tube changes, the efficiency of TWT may get worse, it has to make the electronic energy similar at the situations of large current and the small one. In this paper,an example of radiant cooling space TWT for Ku-band is presented, the total efficiency of traveling wave tube in the state of saturation is above 68.81%, and when the power backs off the half of the state of saturation, The total efficiency is above 61.42%.

Author Keywords: radiant cooling space traveling wave tube

articleTitle: Development of C/X/Ku-Band High Power Helix Traveling-Wave Tube
abstract: This paper describes a 6–18 GHz high-power pulse traveling-wave tube (TWT) developed by Nanjing Sanle Group Co., Ltd, and mainly presents the performance that can be achieved in hot-test experiments at present. This fabricated helix TWT is the continuation of further work based on the previous 8-18GHz 5 kW-level packaged TWT. The high-power prototype TWT has demonstrated over 5.2 kW pulse output power cover 6-17GHz, 4.9 kW-level pulse output power over 17–18 GHz, and the 250 W-average power in the full frequency band.

articleTitle: Design and Experiment of the Electron-Optical System for 0.67 THz TWT
abstract: This paper described the 3D simulation method and results of electron gun and beam transport for the 0.67THz travelling wave tube (TWT) with the help of CST. The hot test results show that the design of the electron beam optics system satisfied the need of the TWT It bases the manufacture of the 0.67THz travelling wave tube.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Ferrite Based High Power X-Band RF Load
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a high-power RF load operating at a frequency 9300 ± 10 MHz with a capability of handling 2 MW peak and 2 kW average power. Several layers of ferrite slabs are used on a straight copper insert to absorb high microwave power. The design parameters and S-parameter characteristics of the load have been analyzed and optimized by using CST Studio Suite. To avoid water leakage, indirect cooling is provided to the ferrite slabs through a cooling channel inside the copper insert. The cold simulation results predict better than 20 dB return loss over a bandwidth of ~100 MHz. The maximum temperature developed on the first layer of ferrite near tip of the insert is 340K for an average input power of 2 kW.

articleTitle: Comparison of Excitation Voltage-Waveforms for Millimeter-Wave Magnetron
abstract: In this paper, we have applied two kind of modulated voltage-waveforms for millimeter-wave magnetron. One of voltage-waveforms is ideal smooth step function, whereas another is a voltage-waveform which is more like a real shoot. 22-vane rising-sun magnetron which operates at Ka-band were used for demonstrated in 3D electromagnetic simulation software. Output RF-power, current-waveforms as well as spectra are compared to reveal the difference of a stable and an unstable voltage-waveform.

articleTitle: 0.22THz Traveling-Wave Tube Based on a V-Shaped Rectangular Groove Staggered Double Grating Waveguide Slow-Wave Structure
abstract: A 0.22THz traveling-wave tube (TWT) based on a V-shaped rectangular groove staggered double grating waveguide (V-RG-SDGW) slow-wave structure (SWS) is proposed. This SWS has the advantages of higher interaction impedance and broadband bandwidth. The high frequency characteristics of the SWS have been studied by CST. The particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation results show that the output power reaches 45.6W at 225GHz under the condition of beam voltage of 21.75kV, beam current of 150mA and input power of 10mW, and corresponding gain and electron efficiency are 36.59dB and 1.4%, respectively.

articleTitle: 3-D PIC Simulation of the High-Power Traveling-Wave Tube with Multiple-Tunnel Meander-Line Slow-Wave Structure
abstract: Development of miniature and high-power vacuum electron devices as sources of coherent millimeter and THz radiation is one of the promising tasks for modern science and technology. Such devices can be applied as radiation sources in modern wireless high-data rate communication systems. This work is concerned with the development of multiple-tunnel meander-line slow-wave structure (SWS) for miniature V-band traveling-wave tube (TWT).

articleTitle: A Mini-Marx Generator Powered by a Cockcroft-Walton Voltage Multiplier for a Compact X-ray Source
abstract: A Marx generator generates a high-voltage pulse by charging lots of capacitors in parallel, then suddenly connecting them in series. In principles, a comparatively lower voltage DC power supply can be used for the charging to achieve the desired high voltage. However, a moderate DC high-voltage power supply is still quite expensive and bulky but not in full-time charging. In this work, a mini-Marx generator powered by a Cockcroft-Walton (CW) voltage multiplier has been proposed to form a more efficient but affordable choice of pulsed high-voltage power sources. For generating a high voltage in a range of 70–100 kV with the mini-Marx generator consisting of 8 stages, a CW multiplier operating up to 10–15 kV is required. A 22-stage CW multiplier with an AC supply voltage of 220 V at 60 Hz is chosen so that it can be driven by household electricity to generate a DC voltage of over 13 kV to charge the mini-Marx generator. For demonstration, a prototype of the 22-stage CW powered 4-stage mini-Marx has been tested with an AC voltage of 110 V at 60 Hz. The CW generator can reach ~6 kV to power the mini-Marx, consistent with the PSpice modeling.

articleTitle: Design of a 250W Ku-Band High Efficiency Space TWT
abstract: A Ku-band helix space traveling wave tube is designed in this paper. The output power, gain, and electronic efficiency are guaranteed by using pitch gradient technology. Then a four-stage multistage depressed collector is designed to achieve efficient recovery of the electron beam. In the simulation design, the output power is more than 250W in the working frequency band(1GHz) Meanwhile, collection efficiency of the center frequency can be more than 80%, except for the sharp decrease at high frequency that reaches 75.58%. The total efficiency is estimated to reach 74% in the working frequency band. A tube based the scheme is being processed and assembled.

articleTitle: Progress of the G-Band Sheet-Beam TWT
abstract: The progress of developing a G-band sheet-beam TWT with periodic permanent magnet focusing (PCM) was reported. The beamstick was assembled and tested, which verified the design of the electron optical system. A transmission rate of 81% for the PCM focused sheet beam was achieved with a total current of 125mA. The high-frequency interaction circuit was also prepared with a novel coupling structure. The first G-band sheetbeam TWT has been tested. A saturated power of 57W was measured driven by a folded-waveguide TWT.

Author Keywords: staggered double vane grating slow-wave structure (SWS)

articleTitle: A G-Band Compact Folded Waveguide Traveling Wave Tube Operating at 3π Phase Shift
abstract: This paper reports a folded waveguide (FWG) slow wave structure (SWS) by operating at 3π phase shift. The FWG SWS is designed to avoid the appearance of 3π stopband. The analyzation of the electromagnetic characteristics and properties are presented in this paper. The small signal simulation shows that 80W average output power can be achieved by a 2-sections beam-wave interaction model. The output signal is stable without obvious oscillation.

articleTitle: Shock-Induced Current due to Charge Impact on a Conducting Surface
abstract: An electromagnetic shock occurs when a charged particle strikes a conducting surface and is removed. Using a line charge model, this paper compares the induced current due to this electromagnetic shock with the classical, electrostatic induced current of Ramo and Shockley. The shock-induced current is found to be negligible for a deeply non-relativistic impact energy but becomes appreciable at mildly relativistic impact energies. The implications of this study are discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis of Frequency Shift due to Misalignment Between Upper and Lower Plates of W-Band Planar Interaction Structure
abstract: In this paper, the simulation has been carried out by HFSS to analyze the effect of misalignment of upper and lower plates of planar interaction structure on the frequency shift in the W-band regime. Driven Modal solution type of HFSS has been used to analyze the effect of misalignment values of 10, 15, and 20 microns.

articleTitle: Design of 220GHz TE01-TE11 Mode Converter
abstract: The mode is very important as a part of high power output system, because the output mode of the gyrotron is usually TEon mode. In this paper, we design a mode converter that transforming TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode to TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode. On the basis of iterative method, pattern search algorithm is used to optimize the parameters of the axis function, and a more efficient modal converter is obtained. Pattern search algorithm can optimize the function in the global scope and get more accurate and effective results. Finally, CST is used to verify that the numerical results are in good agreement with the simulation results

articleTitle: Q-band Helix Traveling-Wave Tube for the Next Generation Wireless Communications
abstract: In this paper, a variable pitch helix slow-wave structure (SWS) is designed for Q-band traveling-wave tube (TWT), and its performance is studied by simulation and experiment. In the operating band (36.5 GHz-41.5 GHz), both simulation and experimental results show that the voltage standing wave ratio is less than 1.4. Under the conditions of beam voltage and beam current of 8.5 kV and 60 mA respectively, the simulation results show that the saturation output power of the TWT exceeds 88 W, and the device efficiency is over 60%. The device efficiency still exceeds 22% when it is backed off 6 dB from the saturation. The experimental results show that the saturation power and device efficiency are above 76 W and 48%, respectively, and the device efficiency is above 20% when it is backed off6 dB from the saturation. The above research results lay the foundation for the next generation wireless communications.

articleTitle: Study of OAM Mode Identification by Electric Field Intensity Measurements at E-band
abstract: Increasing the channel capacity is important task in wireless communication to increase the data rate. Orbital angular momentum (OAM) beam can generate infinite orthogonal modes which can be utilized to increase channel capacity [1]. To use OAM beam in communication, mode discrimination is necessary. Since the individual OAM mode can be identified by its phase characteristics, the mode discrimination through phase measurement is the most accurate. But in order to reduce the complexity of the system, the field intensity-based mode identification may provide an alternative method if possible. The OAM beam has a vortex in amplitude and the center of the vortex has zero power which has the distance irrelevant characteristic. Therefore, the OAM mode identification through the intensity difference between the vortex center and other parts may be possible. We present this method through simulations and experiments using spiral phase plates (SPP).

articleTitle: Characterization of a Duo-emitter Thermionic Diode
abstract: The current-voltage (IV) curve and plasma dynam-ics of a vacuum diode, with a low vapor pressure of cesium, are investigated, in which electrons are thermionically emitted from the cathode and cesium ions are emitted from the anode via surface ionization. Two stable branches on the IV-curve were demonstrated experimentally and computationally using particle-in-cell simulations. Contrary to historical claims both branches were found at voltages above and below the electrodes' contact potential. Simulations indicate that ion-neutral scattering could lead to this observed behavior.

articleTitle: Design of a Quasi-Optical Launcher for a 135/170GHz, Dual-Frequency Gyrotron
abstract: In this paper, the design of a quasi-optical launcher (QOL) for a 1351170GHz 1-MW double-frequency gyrotron is presented. The gyrotron operating at both 170GHz and 140GHz is being designed, then this investigation is on the design of a launcher toward 170GHz and 140GHz dual-frequency gyrotron. The accurately chosen modes and operating frequencies are TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">25,10</inf> for 170GHz and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20,8</inf>for 135GHz. Gyrotrons at these two frequencies can be used for plasma heating applications in Controlled Nuclear Fusion. A numerical calculation code has been written for calculating the related data of the launcher, and LOT was used to simulate the electric field distribution on the launcher's wall. The results show that the energy conversion efficiency of the launcher is more than 99%, Gaussian content factor is more than 85% at the frequencies of both 135GHz and 170GHz. This will be used for the design of a dual-frequency quasi-optic mode converter from operation modes to Gaussian mode.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency S-Band Axial Vircator
abstract: A novel anode design and characterization procedure for a high-efficiency multistage Vircator is presented. A three-dimensional and parametric model of the axial Vircator with a realistic anode grid was created to analyze the interaction between electrons and a realistic anode grid.

articleTitle: Design of an Ultra-Broadband Meta-Surface Output Window for W-Band Confocal Gyro-Amplifiers
abstract: In this paper, a meta-surface output window is designed for W-band confocal gyro-amplifiers operating at HE04 mode. Initial parameters of the window are determined by the transmission theory of multilayer dielectrics based on the principle of equivalent permittivity, and then optimized through full-wave simulation techniques. The ultra-broadband window achieves a transmission of more than -0.15dB and a port reflection of less than -20dB within 75–107 GHz, which is capable of suppressing the absolute oscillation near cutoff frequency of gyro-amplifiers.

articleTitle: Electron-Optic Systems for a Gyrotrons with Multy-Mirror Cavities
abstract: The paper describes some versions of the helical electron beam formation systems suitable to use in the gyrotrons with multy-mirror cavities. Both adiabatic and non-adiabatic systems are considered. Optimization of the electric regimes of the guns as well as the electrode shape is performed. The mentioned systems are aimed to use in new developing now CW gyrotrons of terahertz frequency range.

articleTitle: Research on Two-Dimensional Electrostatic Particle Simulation Method Based on superLU
abstract: In particle simulation, the electrostatic model is used to simulate the physical problems that the electrostatic field plays a decisive role, such as setting the initial electric field distribution of the simulated device, etc. At this time, the Maxwell equations can be converted into Poisson equations. The most critical problem is to solve the Poisson equation to find the grid potential. In the traditional method, we use the iterative method to solve the electrostatic field, but as the electrostatic field environment becomes more and more complex, and the demand for solution accuracy is getting higher and higher. In the case of large-scale meshing, the iterative solution method is difficult Convergence, low accuracy, etc. Therefore, this paper adopts the direct solution method to formalize the difference equation of the Poisson equation into a matrix format, and uses superLU to use LU decomposition to directly solve the potential distribution in the two-dimensional electrostatic model field. This direct solution guarantees the absolute convergence of the result. The calculation accuracy and running time are greatly optimized.

articleTitle: A Novel Ridge-Loaded Sine Waveguide for 0.22THz Sheet Electron-Beam Traveling-Wave Tube
abstract: A sheet electron beam traveling-wave tube (TWT) based on novel ridge-loaded sine waveguide (SWG) operating at 0.22 THz is proposed. The interaction impedance of the novel ridge-loaded SWG and the conventional SWG slow-wave structure (SWS) are compared. The calculation results show that the new structure has a higher interaction impedance than the conventional SWG in the frequency range of 0.21-0.25 THz. The transmission characteristics of the new structure show that the return loss is less than -30 dB and the insertion loss is greater than -9 dB with 52 mm length of SWS in the frequency range of 0.21-0.26 THz. The beam-wave interaction characteristics of the novel ridge-loaded SWG TWT are investigated. The PIC results show that the output power is greater than 65 W, and the gain is greater than 28 dB in the entire frequency range of 0.21-0.24 THz. The maximum output power is 103 W (f=0.22 THz), and the corresponding gain is 30 dB.

articleTitle: Simulation of W-Band Folded Waveguide Traveling Wave Tube with Improved Gain Flatness
abstract: W-band traveling-wave tube (TWT) based on the folded waveguide slow wave structure (FWSWS) is simulated to carry out the high power millimeter-wave amplifier. In order to improve the gain flatness, a positive period step section is inserted into the input section in our design. The whole high frequency system is optimized by our calculation. The particle-in-cell (PIC) results predict that the maximum output power of this TWT is 237W and the gain fluctuation is less than 1.2dB in the frequency range of 90-97GHz.

articleTitle: A High Current Field Emission Triode with Nested Ring Gate and Anode
abstract: A field emission triode (FET) with nested ring gate and ring anode structure is proposed. In order to facilitate fabrication and array connection, the planar structure is considered. The cut-off frequency of this FET is about 318.3 THz and the current is about 120 µA when the voltage of anode is 12V with gate voltage at 3V. According to this structure, an array scheme is proposed to acquire higher current.

articleTitle: Test of D-Band Folded Waveguide Traveling-Wave Tube
abstract: A D-band folded waveguide traveling wave tube was fabricated and tested in this paper. When voltage and current of beam is 18.71 kV and 56.6 mA, the electron transmission ratio is 90%. The hot test results show that the output power exceeds 15.4 W at 152 GHz, with gain of 48.37 dB.

articleTitle: Protecting Dielectric SWS Channel From Charging
abstract: Protecting dielectric slow-wave structures of the high-power TWTs and linear electron accelerators from charging by the scattered electrons is considered in this paper. A helical metallization on the transition channel's wall or a tape helix, welded to the wall, are offered for the protection. The electron gun potential on the protecting helix provides the passage of electrons in the equipotential field. The dispersion equation of the sheath helix filled by the electron beam is converted to the TWT characteristic equation and its analysis shows that at the helix pitch less than its radius and the electron beam voltage exceeding 10 kV, any interaction of the electron beam with the field excited in the helix is completely excluded.

articleTitle: The Impact Response Analysis of High-Frequency Circuit in Microwave Tube Based on Finite Element Method
abstract: As an important part of microwave tube, the reliability and stability of high-frequency circuit (HFC) has always attracted more and more attentions of researchers. Because the working environment of microwave tube is very harsh, such as vibration, collision and impact. Therefore, numerical simulation technique is a necessary for researchers to optimize structures to avoid deformation and fatigue fracture in severe working conditions. In this paper, we developed the Impact Response Simulator module (IRS) of microwave tube mechanics simulation software by using finite element method. To validate IRS, numerical results for a helix slow-wave structure is shown compared with ABAQUS.

articleTitle: Regime of Traveling Wave Amplification in the Oversized Circuit with Nonuniform Grating
abstract: The results of experimental study of the traveling-wave amplification in the oversized circuit with a nonuniform grating, which has increased depth of every third groove, have been presented and discussed. Measured TWT gain versus both frequency and beam voltage is compared with the calculated dispersion. The peculiarities of the interaction of a sheet electron beam with a traveling wave have been discussed for the region of mode coupling. Obtained results show a good agreement with the preliminary 3D PIC simulations.

articleTitle: Study on a Theoretical Model of the Empty Orbit for Atomic Bonding Layer of Graphene Covered Metal Surface
abstract: The surface secondary electron yield of aerospace microwave devices can be reduced by surface treatment including metal coating, amorphous carbonation and roughening. This paper focuses on the treatment of metal coating combined with graphene covered, the effective SEY decrease of which are measured experimentally, and theoretically analyzes the feasible mechanism of reducing SEY behind this treatment operation. A theoretical mechanism of reducing SEY by atomic bonding layer is proposed, consisting of the empty orbit mechanism and an equivalent dipole model, which can offer a theoretical method for reducing surface SEY.

articleTitle: Optimization Method of High Efficiency Collector Based on Energy Distribution Measurement
abstract: The high efficiency multistage depressed collector (MDC) of traveling wave tube (TWT) can improve the energy recovery efficiency and improve the reliability of the TWT. The MTSS-BWIS is not accurate enough to predict the electron beam state at the MDC inlet due to errors introduced in the manufacturing. This paper provides a method to optimize the MDC using constructed electron interfaces which based on measurement of energy distribution of electron beam at TWT-MDC inlet. Simulation experiments were carried out in MTSS-EOS and accuracy of this method got verified.

articleTitle: 3-D Particle-in-Cell Simulation of a Multiple-Beam 0.22-THz Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: The results of simulation study aimed at development of a sub-THz traveling-wave tube (TWT) with a triple elliptic electron beam are presented. The dual grating staggered slow-wave structure with a 100-um-height beam tunnel is designed and its cold electromagnetic parameters are simulated. Hot-test parameters of the TWT are simulated by 3-D particle-in-cell (PIC) code. The TWT is driven by a 3×0.06-A, 21.91-kV electron beam with 75um ×250um dimension of each beamlet. The simulation predicts 25-dB small-signal gain and nearly 200-W output power at saturation.

articleTitle: High-Temperature Contact Potential Difference and Thermionic Emission Analysis Using Kelvin Probe Systems
abstract: Understanding the work function of materials used in vacuum electron devices (VEDs) is an important contribution to cathode research today. This is because a lower work function material has the capability to thermionically emit high current densities at lower operating temperatures, meaning longer lifetimes for the VEDs. Two work function analysis techniques are outlined here: measurement of contact potential difference (CPD) at high temperatures and Richardson-Dushman analysis on collected current density data. Both techniques are performed using a Kelvin probe. The techniques are outlined and data collected on pure tungsten are provided.

articleTitle: 0.34 THz Continuous Wave Microwave Power Module
abstract: Development of a 0.34 THz continuous wave microwave power module is described. It operates in 0.33 THz to 0.355 THz providing an output power over 1 W and a gain over 18 dB. It consists of a periodic permanent magnet focused traveling wave tube and a 20 kV electronic power conditioner. A novel modified staggered double vane slow wave structure is employed in the traveling wave tube to realize wide bandwidth.

articleTitle: Planar Helix Slow Wave Structure for K-Band Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: In this paper, we report the design and the fabrication of a novel planar slow wave structure (SWS) to be used in traveling wave tube (TWT) amplifier. The SWS is designed to operate in K-band. Simulations showed the possibility to have a gain higher than 35 dB at a frequency of 25 GHz with a bandwidth of 1 GHz. A maximum output power of 16 W could be achieved. Several SWSs were also fabricated with standard Printed Circuit Board (PCB) technologies demonstrating the possibility to realize low cost device and have good reproducibility.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of a Sheet Beam Electron Gun for Terahertz SDV-TWTs
abstract: A Pierce-type sheet beam electron gun for a terahertz staggered double vane traveling wave tube (SDV-TWT) is designed, which can achieve high output power and broad bandwidth. With the combination of theoretical design and 3D simulation, an electron beam with uniform cross section can be achieved with beam voltage of 25 kV and beam current of 0.25 A. The distortion of beam edge is optimized by adjusting the aspect ratio of cathode and the focus angle of focusing electrode in width. Moreover, the detail design process is put forward to provide a systematic method to optimize the Pierce-type sheet beam electron gun for arbitrary terahertz vacuum devices.

articleTitle: Q-band 190W Helix TWT with Two Stage Collector
abstract: Q-band satellite communications are increasing daily, utilizing high data rate capabilities, and broad bandwidth. NEC Network and Sensor Systems, Ltd. (NETS) has developed a new high power, broad-band, Q-band TWT that can operate at 190Wcw over 42.5-45.5 GHz.

articleTitle: M-Type Cathode Characterization Using a Kelvin Probe System in Vacuum Chamber
abstract: High-performing dispenser cathodes are an essential component of modern vacuum electron devices (VEDs). Therefore, it is important to quantify their emission performance. In order to assess how well a cathode emits electrons, it is useful to measure the emitting surface's work function, or the energy input required to liberate an electron from the material. A lower work function is desirable because it should facilitate higher emitted current densities and longer service lifetimes. This work presents both emission data and work function measurements collected using a customized Kelvin Probe System (KPS) and one of the most common types of cathodes, the M-type cathode.

articleTitle: 8 MW Light Weight, High Power, Vane and Strap Magnetron
abstract: Stellant Systems has developed a high power, light weight, non-relativistic vane and strap magnetron for a DoD customer. The 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> model easily exceeded the required peak power of 8 MW. A 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> improved version is now being constructed.

articleTitle: Shapelets with Optimization in Beam Optics Analyzer
abstract: CCR extends the recent work on the shapelet method to include optimization of the density distribution. The shapelet method constructs the surface beam current and power densities from a set of particles impinging on 3D surfaces. We will present results by the Nelder-Mead method optimizing on the orders of shapelets and shapelet scales.

articleTitle: High Frequency Circuit for E-Band Sheet Beam TWT
abstract: A folded waveguide (FWG) slow-wave structure (SWS) circuit for a compact E-band sheet beam traveling wave tube amplifier (SB-TWTA) has been designed, fabricated, and cold tested by UC Davis and Elve Inc.
