The circuit is compatible with sheet electron beams and predicted to produce high output power with reduced beam current density, hence suitable for periodic permanent magnet (PPM) focusing and lower voltage operation. The optimized SWS can fulfill the 5 GHz (81 - 86 GHz) bandwidth requirement while avoiding backward wave oscillation. A multi-step, side-out coupler is designed to be compatible with the planar periodic magnetic focusing system. A cold test was performed to verify the circuit performance and effects arising from fabrication errors were analyzed with simulation tools.

articleTitle: Design of Pulse Power Supply for High Current Density Electron Beam Source
abstract: In this paper, a floating voltage pulse power supply has been designed and analyzed for the generation of a high current density electron beam from a pseudospark discharge-based electron beam source. The developed pulse power supply energizes the ferroelectric cathode (FEC), which generates seed electrons in the trigger-based breakdown mode of the pseudospark-based electron gun. The operation of the system is discussed, and it has been simulated in Matlab Simulink. A hardware prototype has been developed, and the major pulse parameters in the simulation and hardware have been analyzed.

articleTitle: Frequency Self-Modulation in the W-Band Gyrotron Traveling Wave Tube Hot Test
abstract: Frequency self-modulation (FSM) phenomenon is observed in the hot test of our designed W-band gyrotron traveling wave tube (gyro-TWT). It is mainly composed of two different groups, which originate from oscillations in the range of 85 GHz to 90 GHz. The observed self-modulation frequency fluctuates between 219.47 and 231.4 MHz. From our analysis, the FSM may be caused by the window reflection combined with the misalignment of electron beam and tilt of the superconducting magnetic. This paper focuses on the changes of FSM under different beam current and pitch factor.

articleTitle: Experiments on Multipactor Suppression in a Coaxial Transmission Line
abstract: Multipactor discharges are capable of damaging and disrupting RF vacuum electronic devices. Developing new techniques for suppressing and preventing multipactor discharges is essential to ensure reliable, long-term operations. We explore two methods to prevent multipactor in a coaxial transmission line by altering the surface morphology. We evaluate the multipactor suppression properties of textured 3D printed versus porous conductor surfaces.

articleTitle: Modified Spectral Approach with Linearized Boundary Condition for Gyrotron Cavity Modeling
abstract: The article proposes a simple method for calculating the complex frequencies and field distributions of lon-gitudinal modes in an open cavity of a gyrotron using a single solution of a matrix linear generalized eigenvalue prob-lem (MLGEP).

articleTitle: CFDTD PIC Simulation of a Dielectric-Loaded Rectangular Waveguide for THz Wave Generation
abstract: The micro-fabrication of small planar or rectangular waveguide components for use at very high frequencies in millimeter and up to THz wave ranges has attracted a lot of attention in recent decades due to advanced semiconductor manufacturing technologies. A homogenous metallic waveguide is a fast wave structure while a slow wave structure (SWS) can be obtained with employing a corrugation or dielectric filling in the waveguide. For a dielectric loaded waveguide, the normal modes are not, in general, either pure transverse electric (TE) or transverse magnetic (TM) modes, but rather combinations of these modes, namely longitudinal section electric (LSE) and longitudinal section magnetic (LSM) modes having no E and H components normal to the interface, respectively. It had been proposed to use a dielectric-loaded rectangular waveguide as an accelerating structure. In this work, we propose to use the partially filled rectangular waveguide as a SWS for THz wave generation (reversed acceleration) since the same beam wave interaction can be employed. The field analysis of the SWS is conducted using a conformal finite-difference time-domain (CFDTD) method and the corresponding dispersion relations of TE, TM, LSE, and LSM modes are calculated. The beam wave interaction for THz generation is studied using the 3-D CFDTD particle-in-cell simulations. The detailed simulation model and calculation results will be presented.

articleTitle: A High-Efficiency, High Average Power, Multiple Beam Inductive Output Tube
abstract: A high efficiency, Multiple Beam Inductive Output Tube (IOT) with an efficiency greater than 80% would substantially reduce the operating costs of next-generation particle accelerators. We discuss the development of a multiple-beam IOT that employs a third harmonic drive component on the grid to achieve efficiencies greater than 80%. We discuss a novel input coupler, grid design, and simulation of the output cavity. This presents a path forward to the design and production of such high efficiency IOTs.

articleTitle: Design of Ka-Band Traveling Wave Tube for Wireless Links
abstract: Ka-band is gaining interest for terrestrial and space communications and the frequency in the range 27.5 - 29.5 GHz is already used in 5G for high data rate links. This paper will describe the design of a traveling wave tube for wireless communication with long range in the band 27.5 - 29.5 GHz. The TWT uses a double corrugated waveguide with triangular pillars. The gain is about 40 dB and the output power better than 200 W

articleTitle: Study on a 140GHz,170GHz Dual-Frequency Gyrotron for Plasma Heating
abstract: 140GHz and 170GHz gyrotrons are both employed in Electron Cyclotron Resonance Heating (ECRH) system in tokamak experiment. This presentation shows an initial resonator design of 140GHz/170GHz dual-frequency gyrotron, which based on the development of 140GHz and 170GHz gyrotron fabricated at BVERI. The TE22,8 mode and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">25</inf>, <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode are selected and the output powers of resonator is 1.04MW and 1.06MW respectively.

articleTitle: Enhanced Linearity with Low AM-PM Conversion of InnoSys' Millimeter Wave Solid State Vacuum Device (SSVD™) Traveling Wave Tubes
abstract: In this paper we report on the enhancement of both the AM-AM and AM-PM linearity of our millimeter wave (MMW) broadband high power traveling wave tube (TWT). Specifically, the linearity of a solid state vacuum device (SSVD™) based E-band TWT that covers the bandwidth of 81–86 GHz with a saturated power of around 100 Watts will be investigated and improved. Our SSVD™ technology employs solid state integrated circuit design and fabrication for the beam-wave interaction circuit slow wave structure (SWS) to realize and achieve high performance MMW TWTs. Specifically, in this paper, we report on our study to improve the AM-AM and AM-PM linearity of some of our MMW broadband high power SSVD™ TWTs to meet the set goal of a targeted 55.44 dBm Output 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order intercept point, in other words, OIP3 with less than 3.2° phase error across the desired broad bandwidth.

articleTitle: A New Method to Improve the Efficiency of High Peak Power Klystron
abstract: High peak power klystron has broad application prospects in large scientific and engineering fields such as microwave weapon system and high-energy electron positron collider. The conventional methods to improve the efficiency of high peak power klystron mainly include second harmonic cavities, long drift tube technology and extended interaction circuits. In this paper, the design method of reducing microwave leakage is adopted to improve the efficiency of 100MW klystron working in S-band instantaneous power by more than 5%.

articleTitle: Experimental Test of the Field Emission Cathode for Low Power Gyrotrons
abstract: We presented measurements results of helical electron beam properties in the electron-optical system with field emission. The difference of transverse velocities of electrons take place versus radial coordinate of emitter ring, but electron beam properties look good enough for excitation of operating mode. The experimental data about velocity spread are in agreement with numerical modeling.

Author Keywords: spectroscopy and diagnostic of various media

articleTitle: Study on the Application of Oversized Horn Antenna in Array
abstract: To obtain high equivalent isotropically radiated power (EIRP) with limited transmission power for an 8 × 30 antenna array with large dimensions relative to the operating wavelength of the antenna element, the dielectric lens is designed as well as a matching layer which is used to reduce the reflection caused by the dielectric lens. 3-D electromagnetic computer code CST is used to verify the design. The simulation results show that the proposed antenna element used in the array has improved 1.8 dB of the gain, and decreased the side lode level from -5.2 dB to -13.4 dB.

articleTitle: Research progress on Double Mode Staggered Double-Vane Traveling-Wave Tube in G-band
abstract: In this paper, research progress on double-mode staggered double-vane traveling-wave tube (SDV-TWT) in G-band has been demonstrated. By using the double-mode operation, SDV-TWT can work in both odd mode and even mode, and the working bandwidth can be further increased. Results show that the double-mode double-beam SDV-TWT has a wide 3-dB bandwidth of 70 GHz, and by using the sheet-beam and the double-mode operation together, 470 W of output power with a wide bandwidth over 60 GHz can be get. These results demonstrate the potential of the SDV-TWT in high power and wide bandwidth terahertz power source.

articleTitle: Adjoint Approach to Optimization of TWT Design
abstract: We show that the partial derivatives with respect to design parameters of various TWT figures of merit may be efficiently calculated by solving the adjoint equations governing the beam-wave interaction in a traveling wave tube (TWT). Figures of merit include average gain, gain flatness, and gain-bandwidth product, and design parameters include beam voltage and circuit geometry. The derivatives are calculated by modified 1D large signal simulation code CHRISTINE-Z and used in an optimization algorithm that finds parameter values that minimize or maximize the desired figure of merit. Only three runs of the modified code suffice to compute the partial derivatives of the output power and phase at a specified frequency with respect to an arbitrary number of parameters, resulting in a potentially large savings in computing time compared with direct, finite difference calculation of the partial derivatives. We illustrate the method by optimizing the beam voltage and gap spacing of a W-band folded-waveguide TWT.

articleTitle: Compact Low-Voltage Klystrons for Integrated Linear Accelerator Systems
abstract: SLAC is developing multiple compact linear accelerator systems, with a fully integrated modulator, RF sources, controls, and the linac structure itself. To minimize the size and cost of these systems, a series of relatively low voltage (~60 kV) high power klystrons have been developed. This presentation will provide an update on the build status and preliminary test results from these compact klystron prototypes.

articleTitle: Hot Electron Laser Assisted Cathode Using Electronically Tunable Negative Electron Surfaces-Prospects and Challenges
abstract: State-of-the art negative electron affinity cathodes are being considered as promising high-frequency photoemitters because of their reasonably high external quantum efficiency and low mean transverse energies. However, their large-scale application is still limited by their instability and complex fabrication process. In this work, we have designed and fabricated an electronically tunable hot electron laser assisted cathode using negative electron surfaces by employing a facile exsitu fabrication technique. Despite the lack of any optimization, the proof-of-concept device has demonstrated excellent air stability and an external quantum efficiency of ~0.5%. This study can provide insight into the prospects and challenges of designing novel negative electron affinity photocathodes with high quantum efficiency.

articleTitle: Study of High Power Uniform Structure Helix Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: A high-power uniform helix traveling-wave tube amplifier (TWT) with T-shaped and half-moon metallic vanes is presented. By loading two sections of concentrated attenuator with a sever, the simulation results show that complete suppression of back-wave oscillation is realized, as well as more than average 3kW output power and 42dB gain within 7–12GHz.

articleTitle: Multi-Modes OAM Beam Generation Based on Reflective Holographic Technology
abstract: A system to generate high-purity multi-mode orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams at 34 GHz based on holographic technology is designed in this article. The system consists a Gaussian horn and two irregular metal reflective mirrors, by which the Gaussian-like beam generated form the feed source can be transformed into OAM beams with various mode. Through theoretical calculation and simulation, the purity of the generated OAM beams reached 91% and 88% with mode +1 and +2 respectively.

articleTitle: Smith-Purcell Radiation with Different Grating Parameters and Beam Bunching Frequencies
abstract: This paper calculates Smith-Purcell radiation (SPR) operating points based on dispersion curves at different grating parameters (groove's heights and widths) with a fixed grating period. The operating point is determined at the intersection of the SPR dispersion and the beam mode, which emits SPR radiation at second harmonics of this frequency. According to the SPR equation, the SPR frequency depends on the period of the metallic grating. The dispersion relation, on the other hand, shows that, in addition to the grating period, the frequency of SPR varies significantly with grating parameters. Numerical analysis using CST Particle Studio shows that when the grating is excited with a beam having a bunching frequency close to the SPR frequency calculated from the dispersion relation, the radiation field has significantly higher strength than excited with beams of other bunching frequencies.

articleTitle: Experimental Research on Output Window of S-Band High Peak Power Klystron
abstract: The output window is an important component for solving the coupling output of high-power microwave. The power capacity and life of the S-band peak klystron output window are tested, The window adopts a long window structure, and the window porcelain adopts concentric grooved alumina ceramic sheet. The window is tested on the S-band traveling wave resonant ring of the Institute of high energy physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences. Its working frequency is 2.856 GHhz and RF pulse width is 2 µS. When the repetition frequency is 25 Hz, it can bear the peak power of more than 120 MW. Through the resonant ring device, the R&D cycle and cost of the high-power output window can be greatly improved, so that the breakdown problem of the output window of the high-power klystron caused by insufficient power capacity can be solved at a low cost.

articleTitle: Low Voltage, Four Beam Ka-Band TWT Experiment
abstract: We present experimental hot testing of a novel low voltage, multi-electron beam, serpentine Ka-band traveling wave tube amplifier utilizing a cathode in an immersed magnetic field. The amplifier is designed to run at 430 mA of total beam current spread across four beamlets in an immersed, zero-compression flow. At present, the device is characterized at 225 mA of cathode current with 95% beam transmission at a maximum output power of 68 W. Using a four-segment beam collector, the beams are measured individually and exhibit good current sharing with a standard deviation of about 3 mA.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Work Function for Scandate Cathodes Produced from Nano-Scandia/Tungsten Composite
abstract: Scandate cathodes represent a next-generation performance enhancement over current state-of-the-art tungsten emitters (i.e., the M-type dispenser cathode). The improvement in performance of scandate cathodes is attributed to a lower work function, which yields longer lifetimes, higher power, and/or higher brightness. In this study, we report on a series of scandate cathode emitters fabricated from a novel nano-scandia/tungsten composite powder. The work functions of the cathode surfaces have been measured directly by contact potential difference using a Kelvin probe. These are the first reported work function values for scandate cathodes to be measured directly (in situ) at high temperatures rather than calculated from emission current density via the Richardson-Dushman equation. Several scandate cathodes were determined to have work function values less than that of standard M-type cathodes, with a difference up to ~ 0.4 eV.

articleTitle: Design and Thermal Analysis of Broadband Output Window for W-Band Gyro-TWT
abstract: A broadband three-layer output window structure with inhomogeneous size for W-band Gyro-TWT is designed and analyzed in this paper. The CST simulation results show that the output window has good bandwidth over 84~104 GHz, and it still has good performance within the allowed assembly error. The window is manufactured showing a -17dB reflection over 80~105 GHz. The thermal analysis of three-layer output window has also been carried out by using joint simulation of HFSS and ANSYS. The simulation results verify that the power capacity of the window is more than 30 kW, while it can reach higher when operating at pulse condition.

articleTitle: A Ceramic Surface Charging Model for Accurate Prediction of E-Beam Trajectory in Field Emission Digital X-Ray Sources
abstract: In a digital x-ray source based on a field-emitted electron beam (e-beam), it is important to control the position and size of the focused e-beam at the anode surface, to achieve required performances. For this purpose, e-beam trajectory prediction is performed using a charged particle optical simulation in the geometries of the designed x-ray tube. In this study, to more accurately predict the e-beam trajectory inside a vacuum-sealed digital x-ray tube whose electrodes are insulated with a ceramic material, we newly introduce a ceramic surface charging (CSC) model into the e-beam trajectory simulation. The obtained e-beam characteristics with the CSC model have been compared with the experimental results, and we found that the proposed CSC model successfully led appropriate to calculation well matched with the experimental tendencies compared to the conventional model.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Interferometric for Low-Loss Nonmetallic Sheet Thickness Measurement
abstract: A low-cost method for measuring the thickness of low-loss nonmetallic sheet is proposed. This method is based on the sensitivity of millimeter wave coherent synthesis efficiency to phase consistency. A4-size paper sheets with 0.08mm thickness were tested using an experimental system with a working frequency at 35 GHz, and the preliminary experimental results are reported. The thickness of a low-loss nonmetallic sheet less than 0.08 mm can be measured at 35 GHz.

articleTitle: Tunable Multi-Mirror Gyrotron for Direct Positronium Measurements
abstract: For the implementation of high-power frequency-tunable sub-THz gyrotrons, we propose to use a quasi-optical 6-mirror electrodynamic system in the form of superposition of three confocal resonators located at an angle of 60 degrees to each other. Such a system provides high selective properties for the operating mode with a quasi-uniform azimuthal structure at half the distance from the center to any mirror. Thus, the rather high efficiency can be achieved with using conventional tubular rotating beams. As shown in 3D PIC simulations, a 6-mirror (triple-confocal) gyrotron can provide 6–10 kW output power in the frequency range of 200–207 GHz. Indicated parameters of radiation is highly demand for applications including direct positronium measurements.

articleTitle: Direct Comparison of Analytically Derived Fedosov Solution with Numerical Simulations of Intense Relativistic Electron Beam Generation in Magnetically-Insulated Coaxial Diode of SINUS-6 High-Current Electron-Beam Accelerator
abstract: The aim of this study is to validate an analytically derived solution for intense relativistic electron beam generation in a magnetically-insulated coaxial diode (MICD), a.k, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{a}$</tex>, Fedosov solution, by numerical particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of electron beam generation in a 3D computer model of an MICD driven by the high-current electron-beam accelerator SINUS-6. PIC simulations of this are performed using the ICEPIC code. The comparison of the analytically derived Fedosov solution with results of ICEPIC simulations of the electron beam parameters show very good correlation to each other.

articleTitle: Automatic Test System for HPM Effect Injection Experiment
abstract: Microwave effect experiment is an important means to study the threshold of core electronic components of electronic equipment. In view of the characteristics of traditional microwave effect experimental platforms, which are mostly suitable for single parameter test, cumbersome process and low efficiency. This paper describes a high power microwave (HPM) effect automatic test system with multiple functions, such as one key test, multi parameter extraction, real-time test data acquisition, automatic analysis of test results and so on. Experiments show that the automatic test system can provide experimental data support for the study of electromagnetic effect mechanism and electromagnetic protection scheme of HPM on semiconductor devices and electronic circuits.

articleTitle: Temperature Measurement and Simulation Comparison of Collector of Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: The thermal finite element simulation model is an important method for the temperature simulation and design of the collector of the traveling wave tube. In this paper, the multistage depressed collectors(MDCs) non-welded of a space traveling wave(TWT) tube with a Ku-band of 150W and a total efficiency of 60% is used to establish a temperature simulation model for the collector of the traveling wave tube, and a thermocouple is used to measure the temperature on the fourth electrode of the collector. The model is corrected based on the measured temperature and the unary linear regression method, so that the model simulation can be used to obtain the true temperature close to the inside of the collector. The results show that the similarity between the calculated results of the revised model and the measured temperature is greatly improved.

articleTitle: Observations of Temperature-Induced Material Transformations in Impregnated Scandate Cathode Samples During in situ Heating in the SEM
abstract: Dispenser cathodes operate in a high vacuum environment when used as thermionic emitters in vacuum electron devices. Although significant materials research has been performed on cathodes in recent years, limitations of techniques or instrumentation have made it difficult to obtain real-time observations of dispenser cathodes in a dynamic (heated) state using high-resolution techniques such as advanced scanning electron microscopy. In the present study, to observe and better understand how cathode materials and morphologies were created, the authors performed high temperature in situ heating experiments on impregnated cathode pellet pieces in an SEM, to monitor W faceting and impregnant behavior during heating, in real time.

articleTitle: Data Feedback and Recalculation Analysis for the Helix of Space TWT
abstract: In view of the difficulty of quality determination for Space traveling wave tube's helix, this article introduces a pitch data feedback tool, which enable automatically using the measured pitch data to correct the simulation engineering model, so that the simulation results of the modified project are closer to the actual product performance and realize performance prediction.

articleTitle: Design and Cold-Test of D-band Planar Microstrip Meander Line Slow Wave Structures and Adaptors
abstract: This paper reports the design D-band planar microstrip meander line (MML) slow wave structure (SWS) model based on probe adaptor and meander line antenna. Proposed MML is fabricated by simplified processes based on lithography and magnetron sputtering. The cold-test is carried out with MML model and THz probe. The measurement results show great agreement with simulation results and the deviation may be caused by the inaccurate simulation model.

articleTitle: Concept of Compact Millimeter Wavelength Range Gyrotron-Based Active Coherent Radar for the Moon and Space Debris Detection
abstract: This paper presents concept of the active Moon radar based on 0.26 THz frequency-stabilized gyrotron. The aim of the project is to demonstrate the possibility of using a gyrotron for millimeter wavelength detection of space objects, which may make it possible in the future to implement radars of the specified range with a high spatial resolution using advantages of coherent radar systems.

articleTitle: Improved Multipactor Coatings Using Atomic Layer Deposition
abstract: Multipactor emission can be a serious issue for vacuum electron devices operating at megawatt power levels. It can lead to catastrophic failure from surface arcs or excessive heating of ceramic windows. Titanium nitride is effective at suppressing multipactor emission; however, sputter coating is not strongly bonded to surfaces and issue related to lifetime have arisen. It's also difficult to ensure a uniform coating over large surfaces. This research is investigating atomic layer deposition (ALD) as an improved alternative to sputtered coatings.

articleTitle: Development of a 50 Watts Ultra-Broadband TWT
abstract: An ultra-broadband TWT have been developed in the laboratory, and the parameters are generally in accordance with the designs and simulations. In the frequency range of 2.7 GHz to 18GHz, the fundamental power can reach above 50Watts. And the current of helix is lower than 10mA while duty cycle is continuous wave. Slightly oversaturated input is beneficial to harmonic suppression at the low frequency side. At the frequency 2.7GHz, the 2nd, 3rd and 4th harmonics are -3.01dB, - 4.85dB and -8.07dB respectively.

articleTitle: Investigation of Two Surface Multipactor with Two-Frequency RF Fields and Space-Charge Effects
abstract: We investigate two-surface multipactor induced by two-frequency rf fields by employing 2D Monte Carlo (MC) simulations and 3D electromagnetic Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations using Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Particle Studio. We analyze the effects of relative strength and phase of the second carrier mode on multipactor susceptibility and the time dependent physics. We observe shrinkage of multipactor susceptibility regions for different configurations of two-frequency rf operation compared to single-frequency rf operation. We characterize multipacting particle trajectories due to mixed multipactor modes induced by a two-frequency rf field. We find that space-charge effects reduce the growth rate of the electron population resulting in the shrinkage of multipactor susceptibility bands.

articleTitle: A 0.65THz Extended Interaction Klystron Amplifier
abstract: A 0.65THz sheet beam klystron amplifier with six extended interaction cavities is proposed. The parametric design has been analyzed, including gap width and period length. PIC results show that the output power reaches 4.7W at 650GHz under the condition of operating voltage and current of 18.1kV and 30mA, input power of 5mW, focusing magnetic field of 0.6T. In addition, the output power over 2W from 648.8 to 650.6GHz and 3dB bandwidth of 1.6GHz.

articleTitle: Conception of a Coaxial Ku-Band Transit Time Oscillator with Novel Hollowed Inner Conductor
abstract: High power microwave (HPM) sources designed to operate at high microwave frequency (such as Ku-Band) are challenging. They have to combine high magnitude electromagnetic (EM) fields with narrow geometric structures due to short wavelength operation. Among potential vacuum electronic sources, the coaxial transit time oscillator (TTO) is of great interest since it is built with small size resonant cavities and the EM power density is depressed. However, the inner conductor of such microwave sources often exhibits important weight especially in the case of solid structure. The proposed TTO demonstrates that the inner conductor can adopt a hollow shape. This contributes to lower the overall tube weight. Moreover, the inner conductor is terminated with an endcap that is optimized to perform TEM to TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> electromagnetic mode conversion.

articleTitle: A High Average Efficiency Depressed Collector for a 140 GHz Sheet Beam Traveling Wave Tube with Low Back-Streaming Current
abstract: The initial design of a high average efficiency depressed collector for a 140 GHz sheet beam traveling wave tube (SB-TWT) is presented in this paper. Based on the spent electron beam extracted at the output port of the slow-wave structure (SWS), a single-stage depressed collector with low back-streaming current is designed by using Particle Tracking solver implemented in CST. Initial simulation results show that the average collector efficiency is 92.64% and the average current back-streaming rate is 0.78%. It is shown that the designed collector is adequate in the design of a SB-TWT with an average high tube efficiency.

articleTitle: Reflective Amplification of Powerful Terahertz Pulse by Relativistic Electron Bunch
abstract: We describe an amplifier based on a principally non-linear effect of reflection of a short photo-injector electron bunch from the powerful wave pulse. This is effective mechanism of energy extraction by the wave from particles, when parameters of the electron bunch (initial energy spread, bunch length and emittance) haven't significant influence on the efficiency of the electron-wave interaction. Two concepts of this process (non-resonant and resonant electron-wave interaction) are described.

articleTitle: Resonance Characteristics of Ridge-Loaded Barbell Cavity with Transverse-Mode Overlapping
abstract: Extended interaction klystrons (ElKs) have great potential to achieve high power and broad bandwidth. In order to further broaden the bandwidth of the output cavity, a barbell resonant cavity structure loaded by two ridges is proposed. This structure allows a uniform distribution of the electric field in two parallel rectangular tunnels. For the double sheet beam with a certain aspect ratio, it can be selected to operate either in the abnormal TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode or in the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> mode. By adjusting the structural parameters, a novel transverse-mode overlapping scheme is presented, which allows the output cavity to provide considerable RF impedance over a frequency range.

articleTitle: Progress on TH1509U 170 GHz 1 MW European Gyrotron Program
abstract: The progress of the Thales TH1509U 170 GHz 1 MW CW industrial gyrotron is discussed in this paper. The tube is currently under test to assess the compliance with the ITER gyrotron requirements.

articleTitle: Efficiency Enhancement for an S-Band Axial Vircator Using 5-Stage Two-Step Tapered Radiators
abstract: An S-band multistage axial virtual cathode oscillator with efficiency enhancement for high pulsed power electromagnetic applications is presented. The Particle-in-Cell (PIC) results of the designed 5-stage Vircator, with two-step negative tapering in the reflectors, carried out by CST Studio suite 2021 simulation code show a peak power value of 5.54 GW and an efficiency value of 13.65% at 2.45 GHz, under a beam voltage and current equal to 520 kV and 20 kA, respectively.

articleTitle: M-type Cathode Emission Degradation Simulation based on Surface Coating Degradation Mechanisms
abstract: Cathodes are key components in vacuum electronic devices (VEDs) which dominate the performance and reliability of the tubes to a great extent. As far as we know, cathode failure mechanisms for M-type cathodes have been studied extensively, and existing cathode degradation models can fit well to measured data in most places, but still have noticeable errors in some places. Among all mechanisms, inter-diffusion & ion bombardment were found to be two main cathode failure mechanisms. In this paper, we show by simulation that both the mechanisms contribute a lot to the final cathode emission degradation mode; and ion-bombardment may lead to earlier knee point time but slower decline of the emission at the end of cathode life compared to inter-diffusion-only mechanism.

articleTitle: Heterogeneous Cathode Work Function Measurement and Interpretation: A case Study with SrVO3
abstract: Work function is a key electron emission property. However, questions remain on how to unambiguously measure and interpret the work function. In this proceeding, using polycrystalline SrVO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> perovskite as an example, we clarify a few key issues in work function characterization. We show that the vacuum level, which is significantly affected by the patch and external electric fields, needs to be carefully selected to obtain a clear work function interpretation.

articleTitle: Study for a 0.34THz Filleted Staggered Double Vane SWS
abstract: A 0.34THz filleted staggered double vane slow-wave-structure (FSDV-SWS) is proposed, which uses an input/output coupler with a short axial distance and has been manufacturing verification along the longitudinal section. The simulation results show that with the operating condition of voltage of 19.5kV, current of 80mA and the input power of 10mW, the output power at 0.34THz reaches 41 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> the corresponding gain and efficiency are 36.2dB and 2.6%, respectively. Besides, the output power of FSDV-SWS surpass 20W in the frequency range of 334-342GHz, and the 3dB-bandwidth is more than 8GHz.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of Annular Beam Electron Optical System Based on Carbon Nanotube Cold Cathode
abstract: Carbon nanotube (CNT) cold cathode has become an excellent candidate material for terahertz (THz) vacuum microelectronic radiation source due to its excellent field emission characteristics. Here, we report the development of an annular beam CNT cold cathode electron optical system. Through parametrically optimized macroscale simulations, the cold cathode electron optical system based on CNT film emitter has been demonstrated to emit up to 85.8 mA circular electron beam at a bias of 14.8 kV, with a high beam current density of 156 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Sc2o3-y2o3 Co-Doped W Matrix Dispenser Cathode
abstract: Replacing the expensive Sc in thermionic cathode with cheaper Y has come to be a widespread concern, but has no substantial breakthrough so far in previous studies. In this paper, several co-doped tungsten matrix cathodes with different weight ratio of Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>:Sc<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> were prepared and tested. The results indicate that addition of Y can enhance the emission performance of cathodes in some specific component ratios of Y to Sc. However, the surface analysis indicates that the added Y are not working as adsorption Y to adjust the chemical potential of O and Ba on the surface of cathode like Scandium, but just promote the generation of Sc.

articleTitle: Effects of Realistic Magnetic Field in Ferrite on the Waveguide Circulator for Industrial Applications
abstract: Industrial rectangular waveguide circulators (WR340), with narrow bandwidths of 50 MHz, are available in markets for a hefty price tag depending upon the frequency range. This paper focuses on designing a partial height ferrite circulator with a homogeneous applied bias field to achieve a wider operating bandwidth of 210 MHz. With the frequency centered at 2.45GHz, insertion loss less than 0.24 dB, reflection, and isolation better than 20 dB can be achieved. The circulator studies usually consider a homogeneous applied bias field to the ferrite in simulation, but this is not the case in actual products where permanent magnets are used to produce the magnetic field to ferrites. Hence, we implement a self-consistent model that provides a non-homogeneous applied bias field to the ferrite to show the importance of considering a realistic magnetic field in the simulation of ferrite waveguide circulators. The design and development are performed using the finite element method (FEM) simulations. In the self-consistent model that applies a non-homogeneous bias field, a bandwidth of from 100 MHz to 170 MHz can be achieved with some geometric modifications from the former design, highlighting the importance of considering a realistic magnetic field.

articleTitle: Study on 220-GHz Confocal Gyro-Amplifer Circuits with Wedges-Loaded Mirrors
abstract: This paper proposes a confocal waveguide circuit with stability-enhanced structure for practical applications. Two pairs of metal wedges attached to both sides of mirror plates are introduced. They have an effect on guiding the radiation wave along the wedge wall, keeping the outward wave from directly coupling back into the circuit region. In this way, the unwanted pipe modes in the vacuum cavity can be effectively suppressed. Results indicate that a tilt angle of about 50° works well to suppress the pipe cavity modes, which is able to improve the stability of gyro-amplifiers.

articleTitle: An Exact Linear Theory of Backward Wave Oscillations in a Traveling-Wave Tube including Space-Charge Effects
abstract: Backward Wave Oscillation (BWO) in a given Traveling-Wave Tube (TWT) design is a critical issue that must be addressed in order for the tube to operate as desired. In particular, the two parameters of interest that must be known to understand and control BWO are the starting DC beam current and the oscillation frequency. In this paper, we propose a modification to the traditional small-signal theory of BWO in light of recent discoveries of an additional space-charge correction term to the circuit mode. The new, exact analysis will be applied to studying a Smith-Purcell Radiator.

articleTitle: High-Fidelity Particle-in-Cell Simulations of Thermionic Converters
abstract: Plasma-based thermionic energy converters (TECs) feature non-equilibrium processes that are best modeled using fully kinetic simulations, and pose challenges in terms of length scales, time scales, and complex particle interactions. We present simulations of TECs using two particle-in-cell software packages which use modern high-performance computing to meet the simulation challenges. Using WarpX, we demonstrate the simulation of a triode plasma TEC. Using Aleph, we present simulations of an ignited cesium plasma TEC, including a large set of multi-step ionization processes. The Cs plasma simulations also demonstrate shortcomings of approximate models used historically.

articleTitle: Correlation of Emission Characteristics of Dispenser Cathodes with Structure of Aluminates
abstract: In this study, we prepared BaAhO4 (BA) and Ba<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>CaAlO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf> (B3CA) aluminates with two different structures by the liquid phase co-precipitation method, and used them to prepare a pressed dispenser cathode. After 100 hours operating, BaWO4 was found on the surface of the BA+W cathode, while Ba3WO6 and Ba2CaWO6 were found on the surface of the B3CA+W cathode. The electron emission test of the cathode shows that the emission capacity of the B3CA+W cathode is 50% smaller than that of the impregnated cathode. In addition, we found that there is almost no electron emission from the BA+W cathode. This result can indicate that the aluminate containing the BA structure cannot be used in the dispenser cathode.

articleTitle: A Multi-Mode Extended Interaction Amplifier
abstract: A new kind of slow-wave structure and a novel extended interaction amplifier (EIA) with multiple operating modes are proposed for the first time to overcome the bandwidth limitation of the conventional single-mode EIA. Its advantages in bandwidth, stability and feasibility are demonstrated by the study of a Ka-band EIA circuit. When a is 2.04 and the operating voltage is 18.6 kV, -1dB and -3dB bandwidth of 220 MHz and 400 MHz (1.2% relative bandwidth) is achieved respectively with an output power of 945 W, a gain of 32.8 dB, an efficiency of 10.2% at the center frequency of 34.08 GHz. The bandwidth has increased dramatically by extending the single-mode operation into the multi-mode operation.

articleTitle: The Hot Test of High-power Ku/K Dual-Band TWT
abstract: Future military communication systems on mobile satellite uplink platforms such as ground-based high-mobility vehicles have strict constraints in size, weight, and power. The platforms require increasing data rate and bandwidth for video/imagery transmissions from small aperture terminals. In order to meet these demands, A Ku/K dual-band helix-traveling-wave tube is developed, which produces 351W minimum output power at Ku-band(0.5GHz bandwidth) and 258 W minimum output power at K-band (1.1GHz bandwidth).

articleTitle: A 1.3 GHz 100 kW Ultra-High Efficiency Klystron
abstract: Calabazas Creek Research, Inc. is developing a high efficiency, 1.3 GHz, 100 kW klystron for driving accelerators. A simulated efficiency of 79% was realized, and the device is being assembled. Details of the design, assembly, and available test results will be presented.

articleTitle: Simulating Defects and Reflections in a Traveling Wave Tube with DIMOHA
abstract: DIMOHA is a many-particle time domain model for traveling wave tube simulations, previously presented at IVEC conferences. We apply this model to study the effects of defects and reflections in the slow wave structure. A ripple effect in saturated RF power and phase shift is observed and compared to measurements.

articleTitle: Experimental Studies of an Overmoded Millimeter-Wave BWO
abstract: Experimental results are presented for a high power backward wave oscillator (BWO). An overmoded slow wave structure (SWS) with a relativistic hollow electron beam was used to increase the interaction impedance and to avoid RF breakdown. The results of experiments with this overmoded (D/λ ≈ 8) SWS successfully produced high power radiation at 78.5 GHz. The rectangular corrugation SWS can be fabricated more easily compared to a sinusoidal one. In order to select a higher order mode as the operating mode, a mode selection technique was utilized. In this work, the experimental results were compared with calculations performed using the MAGIC PIC code; the measured data are shown to agree favorably with simulations.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Characterization of TE62 Mode Generator for W band Gyrotron
abstract: TE <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">62</inf>mode generator is a device for characterizing the internal parts of the Gyrotron before vacuum sealing the tube. Mode generator will help in aligning the mirrors and correcting the output pattern of those mirrors. Using IR camera along with thermal paper and leaf the mode pattern can be recorded. Design was carried out in [1], fabrication and testing are performed in this paper.

articleTitle: Experiment Design of One-Octave Bandwidth Gyro-BWO with Zigzag Quasi-Optical Transmission Line
abstract: Design of a proof-of-principle experiment on implementation of a broadband frequency-tunable gyrotron backward-wave oscillator (gyro-BWO) is discussed. The gyro-BWO under consideration is using a recently proposed interaction circuit in the form of quasi-optical transmission line where the mirrors direct a Gaussian wave beam along a zigzag-like path with vertical and inclined segments periodically spaced along longitudinal z-axis. A static B-field and translational electron velocity are directed along z-axis, so that the electron beam periodically intersects with the wave beam. The resonant cyclotron beam-wave interaction occurs at the regions of perpendicular beam-wave intersections yielding in the cyclotron phase bunching and energy exchange with low criticality to the particle velocity spread similar to a gyrotron. The 3D PIC simulations show prospects of this “zigzag” gyro-BWO in realization of frequency tunable oscillators capable of high power and unique (octave frequency band) tuning in the short-millimeter wavelength range. In the paper, a general layout and results of computer modeling of major experimental components (interaction circuit, electron gun, output microwave system etc.) are discussed for a CW device using a cryomagnet with the B-field of 4–8 T. According to CST simulations, the designed gyro-BWO ensures output of nearly Gaussian wave beam of kilowatt power level at any predefined frequency within 107–215 GHz range.

articleTitle: Simulation of the High Power L-4953 Crossed-Field Amplifier
abstract: Simulations are performed on the Stellant Systems, L-4953 crossed-field amplifier (CFA) in VSim. This is a high peak power <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(P_{out}^{peak}\approx 5 {\mathrm{M}}\mathrm{W}, P_{o\tau,t}^{avg}\approx 3.2\text{kW})$</tex>, moderate gain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(G=11.2\text{dB})$</tex>, pulsed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(t_{pulse}=1.8\mu \mathrm{s},\ f_{pulse}=360\ \text{Hz})$</tex> L-band (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f = 1.28$</tex> to 1.35 GHz), reentrant, backward wave, thermionic cathode CFA. Preliminary simulations predict <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$P_{out}^{peak} \approx 7.5\ \text{MW}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Gain} = 11.7$</tex> dB at operation parameters in great agreement with specifications disclosed b y S tellant Systems. A new Child-Langmuir emission model recently introduced by TechX is tested on this crossed-field device, a nd predicts a n a node current of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{a} = 120\ \mathrm{A}$</tex>, which matches relatively well with the the specified anode current of 100 A.

articleTitle: A Broadband Smooth-Walled Spline-Profile Horn with A Stable Radiation Field
abstract: A stable radiation field of feeder is beneficial to improve the aperture efficiency of reflector antenna. To obtain a more stable radiation field, the amplitude and phase characteristics of the output port modes at different frequencies need to be adjusted. A PSO algorithm combined with the mode matching technology is used to realize the optimized feeder, and a broadband smooth-walled spline-profile horn with a stable radiation field is designed through this program. For the desired radiation field with -10 dB edge illumination at θ = 20°, the bandwidth of the optimized horn is increased by 20% compared with the traditional horn without modifying the modal amplitude.

articleTitle: X-Band TWT Transmitter
abstract: Diversified Technologies, Inc. (DTI) in collaboration with Dynetics Technical Solutions (DTS) has developed and installed a high power X-Band Transmitter into a new radar. The transmitter uses a CPI high power broadband TWT and is integrated with a dish antenna. This presentation gives an overview of the transmitter design and construction.

articleTitle: Enhanced Transmission Phenomenon of a Subwavelength-Hole Arrays Under Electron Beam Excitation
abstract: The phenomenon of the extraordinary optical transmission through subwavelength hole arrays has enormous application potential in photonic devices. When an electron bunch passes through a subwavelength hole array with inner tunnels, the SPR radiation in terahertz band with the above phenomenon will be obtained if the transmission peak locates in the SPR band. Due to the enhanced transmission peak, the spectrum of SPR becomes narrow with an obvious peak.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of Devices for Characterization of Cold Parameters in Self-Assembled Metal Helices
abstract: We describe the design and fabrication of devices for on-chip measurements of insertion and return loss in self-assembled helical slow-wave structures on Si substrates.

articleTitle: Characterization of the Materials, Phases and Morphology Typical of High-Performance Scandate Cathodes
abstract: Scandate cathodes offer the promise, and in some cases, they exhibit demonstrated capabilities, of next-generation electron emitters suitable for high-performance electron guns. However, there remains a knowledge gap related to the materials and microstructure that might be targeted in order to consistently produce scandate cathodes that reliably deliver excellent emission properties. This paper will provide an overview of a multi-year project focused on characterization of the materials, phases and microstructures observed for scandate cathodes that had performed well during close-spaced diode testing. Typical features include highly faceted tungsten grains, the presence of nanoscale barium-containing particles that decorate the surfaces of tungsten grains, and the presence of scandium at the cathode's emitting surface. Additional insights into scandate cathode materials were obtained via large-area mapping of the distribution of elements and phases through the thickness of impregnated and life-tested cathode pellets.

articleTitle: Analysis of Broad Band Inter-Digital Structure for Mm-Wave Traveling Wave Tubes
abstract: Analysis of a broad band planar inter-digital slow-wave structures was carried out for millimeter-wave traveling-wave tubes. The analysis of the structure was carried out using CST-Microwave studio for the dispersion and interaction impedance characteristics. Further the analysis was extended for normalized gain parameter to study the effective bandwidth of the structure.

articleTitle: The Design of W-Band Sheet Beam Electron-Optics System and The Equivalent Theory of PCM
abstract: Using CST simulation software, a sheet beam electron gun with U=33kV and I=0.68A was designed to meet the high-power requirements of the W-band sheet beam traveling-wave tube. The waist size of the elliptical sheet beam is 1.2mm*0.18 mm. The PCM structure with offset pole is used in the matching focusing magnetic system. The results show that in a 1.75mm*0.4mm rectangular channel, the elliptical sheet electron beam can be transmitted 100mm without interception. To shorten the design cycle of PCM, the rectangular current coil equivalent circuit was adopted to calculate the axial magnetic field Bz. The theoretical calculation results are consistent with the CST simulation.

articleTitle: Theory Description and Verification on 0.34 THz Circular Electron Beam Gun
abstract: Based on the theory from V.A. Syrovoy on describing electron beam according to differential geometry theory, this paper investigates a theoretical description of circular electron beam. According to the physical parameters such as input voltage and current, cathode shape and size, electron beam channel size and distance between cathode and anode, the three-dimensional spatial potential of electron beam can be calculated. The possibility to get the electron beam motion trajectories is shown by comparing the theory function potential and the beam cross sections.

articleTitle: Preliminary Design of an 8-38GHz Helix x TWT
abstract: An ultra-wideband helix traveling wave tube (TWT) is designed and simulated in this paper. By comparing two shapes of vane, the helix structure with semi-metallic rods and T-type vanes is selected for this TWT The preliminary simulation results show that the fundamental output power is more than 120W within the frequency range of 8-38GHz, the power ratios of second and third harmonic are below -4.5dB and -6.1dB.

articleTitle: Development of Electron-Optic System with Compression of Multiple Elliptic Electron Beam
abstract: Multiple-sheet-beam traveling-wave tubes (TWTs) for high-power, wideband operation at sub-THz and THz frequencies have attracted a strong interest. Using electron-optic systems (EOSs) with compression allows reduce of the cathode loading and enables operation in a continuous-wave (CW) mode. However, it is difficult to develop an EOS with high compression of a multiple sheet electron beam. In this article, we present the results of development of EOS producing a triple elliptic-shaped electron beam. Two designs with the compression rate of 6.4 and 16, respectively, are presented. The electron guns consisting of an impregnated thermionic cathode, a shadow grid, a planar control grid, and an anode with the beam tunnel are designed and fabricated.

articleTitle: Finite Element Analysis of Slow-Wave System with Rotated Periodic Structure
abstract: Regard to the efficient analysis of the cold cavity characteristics of the space traveling wave tube slow-wave structure (SWS) with a periodic structure, this article briefly describes a rotating periodic boundary condition based on the finite element method, and developed a simulator named high frequency circuit solver (HFCS). To validate it, this article numerically simulate the staggered double grating slow-wave structure with longitudinal and angular periodicity, solve its phase shift frequency and dispersion curve, and compare with the HFSS simulation results

articleTitle: ICEPIC Simulations of Microwave Power Increase from 2.45 GHz Magnetron
abstract: Standard operation of a conventional microwave oven 2.45 GHz “cooker” magnetron with 4.0-4.3 kV of pulsed applied voltages at 0.17-0.19 T magnetic fields results in generation of pulsed microwave power 1.8-2.8 kW, which is recalculated to an average microwave power 0.9-1.9 kW when the “cooker” magnetron operates with 50% duty cycle while driven by a “rectified” a.c. voltage from the wall-plug. It has been shown in many experimental studies of “cold-start” operation of a standard 10-vane double-strapped 2.45 GHz “cooker” that it readily sustains, when properly conditioned, up to ~10 kV d.c. and up to ~14 kV of peak-to-peak a.c. applied voltage with just a few μA cold (field emission) leakage (anode) current. The latter suggests that a standard 2.45 GHz “cooker” magnetron may successfully operate in the desired, lowest mode with much more output microwave power at even higher magnetic fields when driven by up to 10 kV of d.c. or quasi-d. c. appropriate, syn-chronous applied voltage. Results of ICEPIC simulations of magnetron operation at different magnetic fields with appropriate, synchronous applied voltages show that, for example, with 8.0 kV applied voltage at 0.35 T magnetic field, the “cooker” magnetron is able to generate up to 6.0 kW of output microwave power with anode current ~0.9 A.

articleTitle: A 3.0 Mw, 402.5 MHz, Pulsed Klystron for Use in the Spallation Neutron Source DTL-Linac at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory
abstract: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) commissioned Communications and Power Industries (CPI) to develop a new 3.0-Mw, pulsed, 402.5-MHz klystron to use in the Drift-Tube Linac (DTL) of the Spallation Neutron Source (SNS). The new klystron must utilize the existing high voltage oil tank and fit within the available vertical space, while at the same time produce 20 percent more output power than the existing DTL klystrons. To achieve the higher output power, an increase of 4 amperes in beam current would be provided with a reduction in minimum efficiency from 58 percent to 56 percent. Performance requirements and specifications will be presented and compared with test results from the first Engineering Prototype.

articleTitle: Sub-GW Power Spatially-Extended Surface-Wave Oscillators of Cylindrical Geometry with Two-Dimensional Distributed Feedback Operating at Ka and W Bands
abstract: Original conception of spatially-extended high-power Cherenkov masers is under development in IAP RAS (N.Novgorod). Electrodynamic systems of such oscillators are based on 2D-periodical slow-wave structures realizing 2D distributed feedback mechanism, allowing for provision of stable narrow-band oscillation regime under conditions of substantial oversize. The paper describes recent results of theoretical and experimental studies of the Surface-Wave Oscillators (SWO) of cylindrical geometry with 2D distributed feedback driven by high-current accelerator “Sinus-6” 500 keV / 5 kA / 25 ns. In the proof-of-principal experiment carried out at the Ka-band, a narrow-band generation with output power of about 200 - 250 MW was obtained at the oversize factorØ/λ ~ 5. In accordance with the simulations efficient operation of the SWO at the W-band was demonstrated in a narrow-band oscillation regime with an output power of about 150 - 200 MW at the oversize factor Ø/λ ~ 10.

articleTitle: Investigation on Mode Converter Based on All-Dielectric Metamaterial for Gyrotron
abstract: Artificial metamaterials have made great progress in controlling and manipulating electromagnetic waves. However, the common plasmonic metamaterials suffer from ohmic loss, which leads to low transmission efficiency and impedes wide application. All-dielectric metamaterials provide an effective means to solve the ohmic loss problem of the plasmonic-type metamaterials. In this paper, a gyrotron quasi-optical-mode converter based on all-dielectric metamaterial is proposed. Such dielectric metamaterial consisting of alumina ceramics and silica substrates is easy to fabricate, making them very promising in developing low-loss terahertz functional devices. The electromagnetic simulation results show that the designed mode converter can well convert the cylindrical TE01 mode into Gaussian beam. The obtained scalar Gaussian content reaches 98.56 % on the observation plane.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Network Modeling for Traveling Wave Tube
abstract: In order to accelerate the speed of modeling and optimization of traveling wave tubes, this paper applies deep neural network to the design of traveling wave tube. This paper uses the script written by Python to drive 3D simulation software to model and simulate the pill-box window model. Experimental results show that this method can shorten the design time and improve design accuracy. The feasibility of this method in traveling wave tube is verified.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Smith-Purcell Radiation from Bound States in the Continuum
abstract: When free electrons approach the grating, intense Smith-Purcell radiation (SPR) can be generated at resonant frequencies. In this paper, we calculate the analytical solution of SPR amplitude. The results show that bound states in the continuum (BIC) can enhance SPR by several orders of magnitude. In addition, we prove that the combination of BIC and superradiation is two orders of magnitude stronger than ordinary SP superradiation. Our research may advance the development of compact high-power spontaneous radiation sources.

articleTitle: High Efficiency and Low Loss Investigation of an Advanced Dual-Cavity SB-EIO
abstract: Efficiency and loss are the key factors limiting the development of sheet beam extended interaction devices. In this paper, a dual-cavity sheet beam extended interaction oscillator (SB-EIO) with low loss and high efficiency based on one-dimensional computing code is developed. The SB-EIO is optimized by particle swarm optimization(PSO) algorithm and the ideal electron bunching is obtained. Compared with single cavity, the efficiency of Ka-band dual-cavity EIO is increased from 16.34% to 40.53%, and the loss is reduced from 19.46% to 16.45%. The efficiency of W-band EIO is increased from 11.91% to 25.21%, and the loss is reduced from 28.07% to 17.43%. The results show that the dual-cavity has higher efficiency and lower loss than the single cavity, so it is a practical strategy and is expected to be extended to other traditional devices.

articleTitle: Oversized Electrodynamic Systems for Powerful Long-Pulse Sub-THz/THz Band FEL: Simulations and “Cold” Tests
abstract: Project of sub-THz/THz band FEL driven by induction linac “LIU” 5 - 20 MeV / 2 kA / 200 ns is under development in collaboration between BINP RAS (Novosibirsk) and IAP RAS (N.Novgorod) and aimed to achieve ultra-high (sub-GW to GW level) radiation power in this frequency range. In order to provide stable narrow-band generation regime in the strongly-oversized oscillator, we elaborate two types of electrodynamic systems: (1) advanced Bragg resonators based on coupling of quasi-cutoff and propagating waves and (2) quasi-optical resonators of the Talbot-type. Design of these resonators, their simulations and “cold” test results are presented, state of the project is discussed.

articleTitle: Multiple Beam Power Grid Tubes
abstract: High power, high efficiency RF sources are required at frequencies below 700 MHz for ion and proton accelerators. These sources are also used for high energy accelerators, such as the Advanced Photon Source, which is seeking 350 MHz RF sources producing more than 200 kW of continuous power. The program is developing multiple beam triodes to provide this RF power at efficiencies exceeding 80%. The sources would be extremely compact and low cost. Both the triodes and the associated RF cavities are being developed.

articleTitle: A Circular TE02 Mode Filter for Ka-band High Power Millimeter Wave Transmission Line
abstract: A circular TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> mode filter based on the quad-polar waveguide is proposed for the Ka-band high power millimeter wave transmission line. Due to the deformation of the waveguide cross section, an obvious distinction field with a different periodical change on the inner surface of waveguide boundary is formed. By introducing two pairs of long slits between the raised and indented boundary, the undesired TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> mode can be filtered while the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode suffers little attenuation. The results show that the transmission efficiency of TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode is over -0.1 dB, while the attenuation loss of parasitic mode TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> mode more than - 18 dB, in the frequency range of 26 GHz to 40 GHz.

articleTitle: High Power V-Band TWT Development
abstract: As a part of plan to deploy a wideband high-power module (HPM) to very high-throughput satellite (VHTS) network systems, CPI has been developing a V-band high-power TWT amplifier. The first two prototypes designed for 500 W and 250 W levels of saturated output power were fully tested, showing 24 dB gain and more than 5 GHz bandwidth with 50 - 100 % of duty factor. Currently, a 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> prototype is being developed with the plan to release its version compatible with market-demands. This paper will summarize their fabrication processes and test results.

articleTitle: Design of High-Power S-Band Pulsed Magnetron for Linear Accelerator System
abstract: This paper deals with design of a high-power S-band pulse magnetron capable of generating average and peak powers of 4 kW and 4 MW at an operating frequency of 2.998±0.005 GHz. The 16 vanes hole and slot type anode structure is considered for design, in which 3D PIC simulation is used for computation of output parameters, whereas ANSYS workbench is used for thermal analysis. The study shows that the resonating frequency depends on the strap dimensions, strap depth, and height. The temperature distribution on the helix-shaped heater, cathode surface, and anode are analyzed from the thermal analysis.

articleTitle: Structural Static Analysis of Microwave Tubes Based on Multi-level Preconditioner
abstract: Small mechanical perturbations of structures can possibly lead to electrical failure of the microwave tubes and even cause the structures of the microwave tubes destroyed. In order to design the optimal microwave tubes, in addition to ensuring the performance of the main electrical parameters, the reliability of heat dissipation and structural force needs to be analyzed. The displacement field of structure plays a vital role in performance analysis of the microwave tubes. In this paper, a three-dimensional structural static analysis method of microwave tubes combined with three-level preconditioner is developed based on finite element method, which can quickly obtain the structural deformation under force. The numerical results show that the technology proposed in this paper has the same accuracy as ANSYS, and has high-efficiency performance.

articleTitle: Quantum Efficiency of Photoemission from Biased Metal Surfaces with Lasers from UV to NIR
abstract: In this paper, we study photoelectron emission from biased metal surfaces with laser wavelengths from 200 nm to 1200 nm (i.e. UV to NIR), using exact analytical solution of one-dimensional (1D) time-dependent Schrödinger equation (TDSE). The dominant electron emission process and quantum efficiency (QE) show strong dependence on the laser intensity, wavelength, and dc field. It is found that QE can be increased nonlinearly by electronic heating due to intense sub-picosecond laser pulses, with the strongest increase near laser wavelengths at which the cathode work function is an integer multiple of the corresponding photon energy. The quantum model with laser heating effects reproduces previous experimental results, which further validates the quantum model and highlights the importance of laser heating.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Metamaterial Klystron for Accelerator Application
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized metamaterial (MTM) klystron at P-band is investigated. The electromagnetic characteristics of the MTM resonant cavity are analyzed, and the radius is smaller than the conventional counterparts due to the subwavelength characteristic of the MTM. The beam-wave interaction is performed on the MTM klystron constructed by MTM resonant cavities. The simulation results show that when the beam voltage and current are 100 kV and 40 A, respectively, the output power of the klystron reaches 2.12 MW at 714 MHz, corresponding to an electronic efficiency of 53% and a saturation gain of 42 dB. The high-frequency structure of the MTM klystron is 0.6 in radius and 0.9 in length of the conventional klystron, which can be used in proton linear accelerator application to solve problems of large volume and heavy weight.

articleTitle: Multi-Physical Parameter Particle Simulation Analysis of Ka Band Gyro-TWT
abstract: Gyro-TWT amplifier has the characteristics of high power, high gain, broadband and high efficiency in millimeter wave band. The Ka band Gyro-TWT is optimized and designed by using magic particle simulation software. Multi physical particle simulation is carried out for its double anode electron optical system, periodic dielectric loss loaded high-frequency beam wave interaction system, collector mode linear gradient and connected whole tube. The working mode is TE01, The simulation results show that when the center frequency is 29.50 GHz, the working voltage is 80kV and the working current is 15 A, the peak power is more than 300 kW, the efficiency is more than 25%, the gain is more than 40 dB and the bandwidth is more than 4 GHz. The development work is in progress.

articleTitle: Research on Parallel Algorithm of High-Power Microwave Device Simulation Based on MSMPI
abstract: The improvement of parallel computing efficiency is of great significance to the development and research of particle simulation theory. This article first compares the communication efficiency of MSMPI and MPICH2. The electromagnetic particle-in-cell simulation parallel algorithm and dynamic load balancing algorithm based on MSMPI shared memory characteristics are designed. Finally, the parallel test of RKA and MILO was realized by the particle simulation software CHIPIC-3D. The test results show that the two algorithms can significantly improve the efficiency of parallel computing.

articleTitle: Low Frequency Oscillator Circuit Using Si-Gated Field Emitter Arrays
abstract: Si-gated field emitter arrays (Si-GFEAs) are strong candidates for nano vacuum channel transistors (NVCTs). In this work, Si-GFEA die with 1000 X1000 arrays were used to create a Colpitts oscillator circuit. First, transfer and output characteristics sweeps were carried and based on those data, a LTSpice vacuum transistor (VT) model was developed. Then the model was used to develop a Colpitts oscillator circuit. The circuit was experimentally tested where the collector voltage was kept at 200 V DC and the gate voltage was kept at 50V DC. From the experiment, an oscillation frequency of ~ 152 kHz was observed with a maximum amplitude of of Vpp=4.38 V.

articleTitle: Model of Helix Traveling Wave Tube Including the Slow-Wave Structure Dispersion Characteristics and Space-Charge Effect
abstract: An analytical model for the interaction between a linear electron beam and a realistic helix slow-wave structure (SWS) in a traveling wave tube (TWT) is provided. It is a generalization of the Pierce model for the interaction, assuming <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex> one-dimensional electron flow along a dispersive helix SWS, with space-charge effects accounted for. The used phase velocity and characteristic impedance are extracted from full-wave simulations. The calculated gain versus frequency is compared with results from the 1D Lagrangian TWT code, LATTE.

articleTitle: Simulation of Multiple Electron Beam Focusing Electron Optical System by MTSS
abstract: This paper introduces the simulation of an electron optical system for a multiple electron beam focusing system. The software used is the Microwave Tube Simulation Software (MTSS) of Institute of Computer Simulation Technology of UESTC. Multiple electron beams are focused by magnetic focusing. Multiple electron beam array is an 8*8 equal-spacing electron beam array, with a total current of 10 nanoampere, an electron beam interval of 6 micron, an electron beam radius of 1 micron, and a voltage of 4950v. The magnetic system can generate a kind of rectangular magnetic field, which can compress the multiple electron beam array by 100 times or more, and the distortion of the multiple electron beam array after compression is small. The cost, time and memory consumption of the simulation are analyzed.

articleTitle: An Application of Metasurface in U-shape Meander-line Slow Wave Structure
abstract: An meander-line slow wave structure (ML-SWS) loading with metasurface is proposed in this paper. The simulation result shows that loading the metasurface can suppress instability and increase the beam-wave interaction efficiency by changing the E field of the slow-wave transmission line.

articleTitle: Research on G-band Extended Interaction Klystron With Broad bandwidth and High Output Power
abstract: In this paper, a G-band extended interaction klystron (EIK) adopting stagger tunning and mode overlap with ladder-type structure is proposed to achieve high power, high efficiency and broad bandwidth. The high frequency characteristics and electric field distribution ofπ mode and 15/16π mode in output cavity is studied. The appropriate frequency interval between modes is determined by adjusting the length ratio of long and short slots. The PIC simulation results show that the circuit we designed can realize dual-mode operation and complete mode overlap. An output power of 870 W, an efficiency of 18.4%, a gain of 46.4 dB and a bandwidth of 1.32 GHz are obtained. The analysis of fabrication tolerance indicates that less than 2-πm machining precision is required. Numerical simulation results demonstrate the feasibility of G-band mode overlap and its ability to the expansion of EIK bandwidth.

articleTitle: Electrostatic Charged-Particle Guides for µm-Scale Beam-Wave Interactions
abstract: We present charged-particle guiding structures capable of confining energetic electron beams to micron-scale transverse dimensions on the surface of a chip. The guiding structures consist of a periodic arrangement of microfabricated electrostatic lenses. We formulate approximate analytical expressions for charged-particle trajectories through these guides, and we design an example guiding structure based on a mesa (stack) of alternating metal and dielectric layers. The example structure is amenable to modern microfabrication techniques, and we show, via particle-in-cell simulations, that electron beams with energies from 1 keV to 1 MeV and beam current densities> 1 kA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> should be stably confined with guides of this design. These guiding structures may enable enhanced interactions between electron beams and high-frequency electromagnetic waves for applications in THz-frequency vacuum electronics or light-driven accelerators.

articleTitle: Vacuum-Channel Field Emission Transistor Array with Comb-Type Gate
abstract: With advances in integrated circuit manufacturing technique, the miniaturized vacuum electronics come back to the vision of researchers. Vacuum-channel field emission transistor (VFET) is a major area of interest and has potential to be alternative of MOSFET in the high-frequency circuit design. The specific objective of this study was to propose a novel structure of VFET array based on double side gates controlling. The simulation results show that the maximal current can be up to 21.84uA when the voltage on gate and anode are respectively set to 12Vand 15V.

articleTitle: K-Band Helix TWT for NASA Artemis Project
abstract: NEC Network and Sensor Systems, Ltd. has developed a K-band (22.5-23.5GHz) 400Wpeak/300Wcw Traveling Wave Tube (TWT). This paper outlines the challenges for the K-band TWT development, and the development process and key methods implemented to develop a robust and reliable TWT without the need for trial production with proto-type models.

articleTitle: Study of Two-Beam Loading on an Input Cavity for High Power Ka-Band Klystron
abstract: The applications of two beams in klystrons permit a significant increase in the output power at millimeter-wave frequencies. The two-beam loading on input cavity designed to operate in TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</inf>-2π mode is analyzed and optimized to achieve optimal matching condition for certain power of an input signal. To demonstrate the matching condition, particle-in-cell simulations are conducted to calculate the relationship between the saturated gap voltage and frequency of the input signal as a function of the total perveance. Simulation results show that over 99 % of the input RF power can be absorbed by the designed input cavity when the resonant driving frequency is around 35 GHz and the total perveance is 0.539 µP.

articleTitle: Design of Uniform Intensity Field Forming System Based on Improved G-S Algorithm
abstract: A system designed for uniform intensity field forming at 35 GHz is proposed in this paper. The system is constructed with a Gaussian feed and a metallic reflector with specific contour. To increase the uniformity of the field, weight factor has been introduced to the Gerchberg-Saxton algorithm. The result of numerical calculation and simulation shows good agreement, with the scalar purity up to 97.8%, and the center amplitude non-uniformity low to 4.6%. The designed system has potential in improving aperture efficiency of reflect-array antenna.

articleTitle: Development of a S-Band High Power Amplifier Klystron
abstract: JSC Research and Production Corporation “Toriy” has designed and manufactured the KIU-278, a high peak power S-band klystron. The klystron operates in the frequency range 2846–2866 MHz with 8.0 MW peak output power and gain of 50 dB at cathode voltage no more than 58 kV.

articleTitle: C-band Engineering Test Facility: A New High Gradient Breakdown Test Stand at LANL
abstract: This paper describes the current status of the newly commissioned C-band Engineering Test Facility in New Mexico (CERF-NM) at Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL). At LANL, we designed and assembled a new test stand with the goal to conduct high gradient breakdown studies at C-band frequencies (5.712 GHz). The test stand is powered by a 50 MW, 5.712 GHz Canon klystron. It is capable of conditioning single cell accelerating cavities for operation at surface electric fields in excess of 300 MV/m. The first two C-band cavities have just undergone the high power testing and operation at high gradients was demonstrated. Probabilities of breakdown were measured as functions of the peak surface fields. Currently the high gradient cavities are operated at room temperature, but we consider adding a capability for cryogenic operation with a cryo-cooler. The test stand is operational and is open to collaborators.

articleTitle: A 71-76GHz TWTA For Wireless Communication
abstract: A 71–76GHz CW traveling wave tube amplifier for high-data-rate wireless communication has been developed in BVERI. The power amplifier can provide over 40 W output power and 17.6% overall efficiency with two-stage depressed collector. The dimension and weight of the amplifier are 38cm x20cmx7 cm and 6 kg respectively with - 48VDC electronic power conditioner embedded.

articleTitle: High Power High Frequency Space Traveling-Wave Tube
