abstract: In satellite systems, on-board repeaters shall deliver always more RF power at higher frequency to increase satellite capacity for higher data transmission rate. To meet this demand, Thales AVS France has developed two new Traveling Wave Tubes (TWTs): a wideband, high efficient 250 W in Ka-band and an 80 W in Q band. Both TWTs have been qualified in conduction cooled version (THL20250C, THL40080C), the end of the qualification of a radiation cooled version in Ka-band (THL20250R) being planned in Q1 2022. The main technical characteristics of the THL20250 and THL40080 family are described as well as the main performances in Ka-band and Q band.

articleTitle: The 3D Study of the Hybrid Bulk-Surface Eigen Modes in the THz Cherenkov Oscillator
abstract: The properties of hybrid bulk-surface modes have been studied and their potential for the efficient interaction with wide sheet electron beams in the THz range has been shown. Main emphasis is put on the interaction of the transverse fundamental and higher modes with respect to the grating width.

articleTitle: Experiment of a Grid-Controlled Electron Gun for the Reversed Cherenkov Radiation Oscillator
abstract: In this paper, a grid-controlled electron gun is experimentally proved to be feasible to generate a pencil electron beam for the reversed Cherenkov radiation oscillator (RCRO). The voltage difference of the heater and cathode is 10.8 V and the heater current is 2.78 A. The working temperature of the cathode surface is ~ 1100 °C. When the voltages of cathode are changed from -24 kV to -26.5 kV, and the voltage differences between the control grid electrode and cathode change from 10 V to 430 V, the measured beam current is changed from 1.2 A to 6.8 A, which means it's really feasible for the RCRO. The RCRO can be applied to large-scale scientific facilities, medical imaging, microwave heating, microwave disinfection and sterilization, and so on.

articleTitle: G-Band Wide-Bandwidth Traveling-Wave Tube Based on Sine Waveguide
abstract: A G-band phase-velocity-taper Sine waveguide traveling wave tube (TWT) with circular electron beam is proposed to amplify terahertz millimeter waves, based on the characteristics of a sine waveguide with wide bandwidth and low loss. In the design work, the high frequency system of the traveling wave tube was first designed, including the slow wave structure, the input/output coupler, connectors and the attenuator. Finally, the injected wave interaction model is calculated. The results show that the tube with phase taper structure can produce over 21W output power and 33dB gain at typical frequency 220GHz with an operating voltage of 17.2 kV, a current of 0.035A, and an input power of 10mW. In the range of 214GHz to 226GHz, the output power is more than 14W and the gain is more than 28dB.

articleTitle: Dielectric Loss Dissipation and Power Capacity Analysis for W Band Gyro-TWT
abstract: The dielectric load Gyro-TWT is a primary high power millimeter source, and its power capacity is limited by the dielectric temperature induced by the RF attenuation. The heavy outgassing was observed when the Gyro-TWT operated in long pulse length in the experiment. The heat dissipated on the dielectric and its distribution is analyzed. Then the thermal performance for the different operating conditions is investigated. And the average power capacity in different pulse lengths is evaluated.

articleTitle: Mitigating Cathode Overcurrent Faults at the Spallation Neutron Source
abstract: The high-power klystron amplifiers at the Spallation Neutron Source (SNS) have been in operation for over 100,000 hours. Overcurrent faults from the klystron cathodes comprise the bulk of RF System downtime. Reliable operation is of particular interest to the SNS, and data from over a decade of operation is used to help mitigate repetitive overcurrent conditions.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation on D-Band Broadband Mode Converter for Gyro-TWT
abstract: The broadband input coupler of D-band TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode gyro-travelling wave tube (TWT) is designed, which transform the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode in the rectangular waveguide to TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode in the circular inner waveguide. The mode converter with 4-slots and 5-slots are designed and discussed. The design of the input coupler is optimized by using CST to get minimum reflections, maximum transmission. The CST simulation results predict that the input coupler offers a good transmission and low reflection at D-band. The -3dB bandwidth is about 11 GHz.

articleTitle: A Discrete Cavity Analysis for Coupled-Cavity Travelling Wave Tubes
abstract: A discrete cavity model is presented here to study coupled cavity travelling wave tubes. Such discrete cavity analysis allows us to treat individually tunable cavities, which was not possible with classical Pierce's analysis. An eigen-analysis method is used to get cold-tube dispersion relationship for a 4 cavity and a 20 cavity system, where the effects of cavity coupling are examined. The model is then extrapolated to include the electron beam, and the hot-tube results for a simple two cavity system are presented.

articleTitle: Inverse Design of Folded Waveguide SWS with Bidirectional Fully Connected Neural Network
abstract: We report on the design and demonstration of a practical Bidirectional Fully Connected Deep Neural Network for folded waveguide (FWG) slow-wave structures, which can be used to speed up the design process of FWG-SWS with excellent performance. The neural network trained to design FWG-SWS using exact numerical simulation results in a form of supervised learning, which shows that the training loss is lower than 0.07. The simulation results show that the transmission of the structure designed by neural network is higher than -0.1 dB at 850GHz center frequency with the phase velocity and the pierce impedance is 0.261c and 24.29 R, respectively.

articleTitle: Dual Recirculating Planar Crossed-Field Amplifier
abstract: A novel Dual Recirculating Planar Crossed-Field Amplifier (RPCFA) has been designed at the University of Michigan. In simulations, the Dual RPCFA has an increased effective bandwidth and operating gain when compared to the RPCFA. Feedback between the two slow-wave structures can be mitigated by adding a smooth bore region before the input of each structure. Experiments will focus on two slow-wave structure designs.

articleTitle: Preliminary Optimum Design of Process Parameters of Transient Liquid Phase Welding
abstract: Transient liquid phase welding process is usually used to prepare vacuum envelope of travelling wave tube with periodic permanent magnet focusing. In the paper, the preliminary optimum design of process parameters of transient liquid phase welding was performed. The key process parameters, which include soaking temperature, soaking time, and working pressure, were studied. Element maps across welding interface were analyzed in order to assess quality of the prepared joints.

articleTitle: Research on Smith-Purcell Radiation Characteristics of Cylindrical Metallic Grating
abstract: We use the waveguide array theory to derive the reflection coefficient of the cylindrical metallic grating, and then through numerical analysis, the dispersion curves are obtained to study the characteristics of the generated Smith-Purcell radiation (SPR). The results show that bound states in the continuum (BICs) and strong resonance exist in the generated SPR. The reflection coefficients at BICs and strong resonance are very high. It provides a promising way for the development of terahertz sources.

articleTitle: Design and Research of a 150GHz Extended Interaction Oscillator with Sheet Beam Working in High-order Mode
abstract: In order to obtain a high-power radiation source in the THz band, this paper designs a 150GHz the extended interaction oscillator (EIO) that works in TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</inf> mode, which is driving by a sheet beam. The cold cavity characteristics and thermal cavity results of the designed EIO is calculated by CST The results show that the DC electron injection voltage is 48kV, and the current is 4A. Electronic injection size of 2.00 mm ×0.20mm can be obtained in high order mode TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">31</inf>, 150GHz. Considering material losses, the conductivity is set to 5.8 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> Sim for copper, output power up to 7.7kW, efficiency is about 4.01%. The designed EIO is of great significance for obtaining terahertz band radiation sources.

articleTitle: A Novel Coplanar Double V-shaped Slow-wave Structure for E-band Backward-wave Oscillator
abstract: A novel coplanar double V-shaped meanderline slow-wave structure (SWS) for E-band backward-wave oscillator (BWO) is proposed in this paper, which is supported by three dielectric rods. The dispersion and transmission characteristics of the SWS have been analyzed. Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulation results for a BWO based on the proposed SWS show a tunable frequency range of 10.1 GHz and a maximum output peak power of 48.9 W at 70 GHz and the corresponding electronic efficiency of 6.0%.

articleTitle: Dielectric Characteristic Measurement of Gyrotron Output Windows
abstract: Some dielectric films of different materials made in China, such as beryllium oxide, aluminum nitride and MPCVD diamond, were measured to obtain the permittivity and loss tangent by free-space transmission measurement method for analyzing and comparing their dielectric characteristics. The results show that the loss tangents of the diamonds can be 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> magnitude, even smaller.

articleTitle: Design and Measurement of a Novel Overmoded TE01 Mode Converter for a Rectangular Gyro-TWT
abstract: In this paper, a sidewall coupler method is adopted to excite an overmoded TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode for the operation of a rectangular gyrotron traveling wave tube. Based on the magnetic dipole moment theory, the coupling aperture is designed and optimized. The rectangular TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n0</inf> (n=2, 3,…) modes are suppressed and the topology can also be applied to excite a TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode with a larger wide side. To verify this design, the novel Ka-band mode converter was manufactured and tested. The back-to-back measurements indicate that the port reflection is lower than -10 dB, and the transmission coefficient is great than -2.4 dB between 33 to 37 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a 140 GHz Sheet Beam Traveling-Wave Tube with a Cuttoff Sever
abstract: Oscillation suppression is one of the most critical issues in the design of sheet beam traveling wave tubes (SBTWTs). This paper adopts a cuttoff sever with a matching step and a Bragg reflector in the interaction circuit, to suppress the oscillation of the sheet beam staggered double-vane (SDV) SBTWT. At the same time, this scheme avoids potential risks caused by the traditional dielectric attenuation. Simulation results show the feasibility of this scheme in the design of a SBTWT.

articleTitle: Main Approaches to Suppress Velocity Spread in the Gyrotron Helical Electron Beams
abstract: The paper presents short overview of the most frequently used ways to diminish the so-called position velocity spread as well as the spread caused by the influence of the own beam space charge in powerful axial-symmetric gyrotrons, where the mentioned above factors strongly affect the oscillatory velocity distribution of the helical electron beams. Some examples of magnetron-injection guns for different tubes operating in various frequency range and power are presented. The efficiency of different methods to suppress velocity spread depending on the technical limitations, operating frequency, beam current and voltage are discussed.

articleTitle: 340GHz EIK Electron-Optical System with High Compression Ratio
abstract: This paper focuses on the design of 340GHz EIK electron-optical system. In order to achieve the pulse output power of 40W, a Pierce circular electron gun with voltage of 20KV, current of 204mA, area compression ratio of 247, was designed by using Ovcharov theory and CST software. ANSYS MAXWELL 2D was used to quickly design the uniform magnetic focusing system, and the results were imported into CST for joint debugging of electron-optical system. With 0.79T focusing magnetic field, the radius of electron beam in the range of interaction length is less than 0.08mm, which meets the interaction requirements. Then the corresponding three-dimensional uniform magnetic focusing system is established through CST for the joint simulation of three-dimensional electron-optical system. The electron trajectories calculated under one-dimensional and three-dimensional magnetic fields are compared and found to be in good agreement.

articleTitle: Study on a Microfabricated Slow-Wave Structure for the Millimeter-Band Backward-Wave Oscillator Based on the Pseudospark-Source Electron Gun
abstract: The truncated sine-waveguide slow-wave interaction structure for the high-power millimeter-band backward-wave oscillator with a pseudospark-sourced sheet electron beam was fabricated using CNC micromilling. The results of morphology studies by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), optical microscopy, and stylus profilometry demonstrate good dimension tolerance and surface quality suitable for operation in the millimeter band. Electromagnetic parameters of the fabricated slow-wave interaction structure were measured in Q-, V-, and W-bands using a vector network analyzer with frequency converters. The results of experimental studies show good transmission and reflection characteristics. Dispersion characteristic was also experimentally measured and compared with numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Field Emission Characteristics of GaN Arrays
abstract: GaN field emitter arrays are being studied for use as vacuum channel transistors (VCTs). In this work, arrays of 150 x 150 GaN field emitters were characterized before and after UV exposure. Collector voltage was kept at 200V DC, and the gate voltage was swept from 0 to 60V. From the I-V measurements, a jump in emission current, a form of conditioning, was observed after a few voltage sweeps resulting in a stable emission current. After UV exposure at 185 nm with 350μW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 5 times increase in current was observed, reaching a maximum field emission current of 6μA.

articleTitle: Power Generation in a Pulsed Plasma Thermionic Diode Using a Barium Dispenser Cathode
abstract: Net output power of up to 0.71 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W/cm^{\wedge}2$</tex> has been achieved in a developmental thermionic converter, using a barium dispenser cathode for high emitter current density, cesium vapor for low collector work function and a high frequency pulsing scheme for efficient excitation of a xenon plasma to reduce space charge.

articleTitle: Experiment on Gyrotron Traveling Wave Tube with Inner Mode Converter in W-band TE02 Mode
abstract: This paper explicates the experimental research of W-band <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TE_{02}$</tex> mode gyrotron traveling wave tube interaction, discussing the reasons for adopting TE02 mode as the working mode, the existing competitive modes, the high-frequency structure adopted, the simulation of the interaction, and the design of the inner mode converter. Finally, the test results are given.

articleTitle: Development of Components of Multi-beam based E-band TWT
abstract: Orbital angular momentum (OAM) is an emerging technology in microwave wireless communication. However, because of high divergence angle of OAM beam in free space, the communication distance is limited and becomes very short. One solution for long distance OAM communication with a compact system is a multi-beam-based high power traveling wave tube (TWT). The multi-beam based TWT can be used to multiplex OAM modes with compensation of OAM path loss in free space. In this paper, for a first step of OAM communication, a dual beam TWT amplifier is designed in E-band. The CST simulation results show that the dual beam based TWT circuit with a bandwidth of 82–86 GHz yielding the output power of over 40 W. The target operating voltage is 11 kV, and the maximum efficiency is calculated as 7.66 % at 85 GHz by CST simulation.

articleTitle: The New Precision Bead-Pull Bench at Thales
abstract: The frequency range of space TWTs is extending to higher frequencies, 32 GHz for space probes, and 40 GHz (Q-band) for telecommunications. Bead-pull is a well-known technique [1] to characterize the propagation parameters along the helix of the TWT. Due to the very small dimensions of the helices at these frequencies, we need to upgrade the bead-pull test bench. In this poster, we present the new bench with higher precision, which is able to address these bands. Compared to previous bead-pull benches, we introduced transverse actuators in order to accurately position the probe on the axis.

articleTitle: Enhancing Radiation of Grating by Defect Structure
abstract: The mechanism of the enhanced Smith-Purcell radiation from a grating with rectangular defects is studied. Through particle in cell simulation, the results show that a grating with rectangular defects can generate stronger radiation. When the defect depth is 70 μm, it can reach about 3 times the radiation power of the traditional grating. It provides a method to increase the radiation power of grating in terahertz region.

articleTitle: Study of Coaxial Magnetron for X-Band Linear Accelerator
abstract: In this article, PIC simulation study of an X- band coaxial magnetron use for Linear Accelerator (LINAC) has been performed. The 40-vane anode resonator along with high quality factor coaxial cavity is designed to operate the device at 9.3 GHz frequency. Further, the generated RF power is couple out to the standard WR112 waveguide through a slot at the outer surface of the coaxial cavity. With the typically selected electrical parameter of 36 kV of voltage, 96 A of current and 0.5625 T of magnetic field, the device generates 2 MW peak power with overall device efficiency of ~57.8%.

articleTitle: Investigation on G-Band Array Sheet-Beams Meander-Line Backward-Wave Oscillator
abstract: A 0.18 THz backward-wave oscillator with array sheet-beams is proposed. The high frequency characteristics of the proposed SWS are studied. PIC simulation results show that the output power of 15 W has been achieved at 186 GHz with an electron efficiency of about 1.3%. The study of frequency versus beam voltage shows that the proposed BWO can be tunable in the frequency range of 181.5 GHz - 189.5 GHz and the output power is higher than 7 W.

articleTitle: Beam Dynamics Modeling of an Electron Gun for an L-Band High-Efficiency IOT
abstract: We show results of 3D space-charge beam dynamics simulation of an L-Band inductive output tube (IOT) rf electron gun. These results are essential to optimize the interaction circuit potentially achieving 100 kW of average power with upward of 80% power efficiency.

articleTitle: Quasi-Analytical Theory of Gyro-BWO with a Zigzag Electrodynamic System
abstract: We describe the small-signal theory of a backward-wave gyro-oscillator with a sectioned quasi-optical system with the zigzag path of the operating wave. This theory explains peculiarities of changing the operating frequency and power of the output signal in the process of the broadband frequency tuning provided by changing the operating magnetic field.

articleTitle: Generation of 565 MW of X-Band Power for Structure-Based Wakefield Acceleration Using a Metamaterial-Based Power Extractor
abstract: This work presents the generation of 565 MW of power at 11.7 GHz with a metallic metamaterial-based power extractor for structure-based wakefield acceleration (SWFA). To our knowledge, this is the highest power level reported in an SWFA experiment. Metamaterial use in a power extractor design allows the structure to overcome some of the limitations faced by other SWFA techniques. Two previous experiments, Stage I in 2018 and Stage II in 2019, have successfully demonstrated the functionality of this approach by generating high power pulses using the 65 MeV electron beam at the Argonne Wakefield Accelerator (AWA) facility. Here, we cover the design and results of the Stage III experiment. The Stage III structure includes significant improvements to increase output power, including an all-copper structure, fully-symmetric output coupler design, and breakdown risk-reduction treatment.

articleTitle: Development of a Cryocooler Driven RF Cavity Test Facility
abstract: Copper accelerating structures performance could be improved by cooling the cavity below liquid nitrogen temperatures (~77K). Below this threshold, the material properties change to support higher RF fields, leading to potentially higher accelerating gradients. Our team has developed a cryocooler-driven testing facility capable of reaching ~10K to perform cryogenic tests of Cu accelerating structures and results from the cooling tests of a 5.1 GHz Cu cavity will be presented here.

articleTitle: Realization Method of Permanent Magnet Focusing System for Improving Electron Injection Flow Rate in High-Frequency Traveling-Wave Tube
abstract: This paper introduces and verifies an efficient implementation method of a high frequency traveling wave tube permanent magnet focusing system based on MFS software. According to the single-loop value of the magnetic field simulated by MFS, the method is used to magnetize and demagnetize each magnetic steel once and then splice it to obtain a magnetic system that meets the design requirements. The electronic focusing effect and circulation of the magnetic system processed by the method can better meet the design requirements.

articleTitle: Interaction of an Electromagnetic Wave with a Counter-Propagating Electron Beam Under the Condition of Cyclotron Resonance Absorption: Nonlinear Periodic Waves, Modulation Instability, and Generation of Solitons
abstract: Transmission of a monochromatic wave through a counter-propagating electron beam under the condition of cyclotron resonance absorption is studied by theoretical analysis and numerical simulation. The nonlinear dispersion relation is derived showing that with an increase in the incident wave power, the non-transmission band shifts to lower frequencies, so wave propagation without attenuation becomes possible. We demonstrate that this propagation is accompanied by the modulation instability (MI), which leads to the wave disintegration into envelope solitons. When the wave frequency increases, the MI changes its nature from absolute to convective, and the generation of soliton trains is replaced by the steady-state transmission. We derive explicit stationary solutions, which turn out to be periodic and are expressed in terms of elliptic Jacobi functions. In the limit of an infinite period, they turn into bright or dark soliton solutions. The theoretical predictions are verified by numerical simulations. The simulations confirm that the boundaries of the non-transmission band are determined by the parameters of the bright and dark solitons. In this way, we obtain the practically interesting analytical condition for the parameters of the incident monochromatic wave, under which the system generates a close-to-periodic train of microwave soliton pulses.

articleTitle: Emission Imaging as Cathode Research Tool
abstract: The idea of cathode emission imaging can be traced to the old days of poor quality oxide cathodes. Back then, it helped in sorting out CRT problems. Today, it turns out, emission imaging of LaB6 and Schottky cathodes may come quite handy as well. We'll show how emission imaging applies to e-beam lithography cathodes development.

articleTitle: Particle Simulation for the X-Band Multi-Injection Klystron
abstract: Researched the effects of the distance of the drift tub head gap of the X-band multi-injection klystron and the radius and height of the resonant cavity on the frequency and quality factor of the resonant cavity, and give a method to suppress the electron backflow of the collector of the X-band multi-injection klystron, Finally, simulated the X-band multi-injection klystron tube by particles simulation, when the input voltage is 21.4kV, the measured cathode current is 16.7A, the conductivity is 2.2f1p, in terms of output, the average power is 57.44KW, the frequency is 9.75GHz, and the gain is about 37.28dB.

articleTitle: Design and Test High-Frequency System of G-Band Folded Waveguide Traveling-Wave Tube
abstract: 220GHz is a very meaningful and valuable atmospheric window frequency band in the low frequency band of the terahertz field. In this paper, the high-frequency system of a G-band folded waveguide traveling wave tube is designed and tested. The simulation results show that under the conditions of working voltage 19460V and current 40mA, the gain is greater than 30dB in the frequency range of 214-224GHz, and the output power is greater than 15W. The high frequency system is processed, and the cold test results show that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}$</tex> is less than -10dB in the frequency range of 205-240GHz.
